definition_zh: 因为；由于；因为（引出理由的从句）
definition_en: for the reason that
core_image: 两条线一头连在一起，后面那条就是前面那条的缘由
scene: 早晨下起大雨，球赛只好取消。The match was cancelled because it rained.
sceneCN: 这里 because 是「因为」（第 1 个义项：引出原因的连词）；句意为因为下雨，比赛被取消了。

derivatives.zh: 由 because 与 of 组合而成，义为「由于」，后接名词或短语
同源名词，义为「原因；事业」，是 because 的后半部分来源

senses.title: For the reason that
senses.definition: used to introduce the reason for something, before a clause
senses.definitionCN: 用在一个从句前，引出某事的原因
senses.example: The match was cancelled because it rained.
senses.exampleCN: 因为下雨，比赛被取消了。
senses.why: The word is built from by plus cause, so its whole job is to place the cause beside the result.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 by 与 cause 合成，它的全部作用就是把「原因」放在结果旁边。

senses.title: Answering a why question
senses.definition: used to give the answer when someone asks why
senses.definitionCN: 在别人问「为什么」时用来说明理由
senses.example: Why are you late? Because the bus broke down.
senses.exampleCN: 你为什么迟到？因为公交车坏了。
senses.why: When the reason stands alone as an answer, the same word carries it without a main clause in front.
senses.whyCN: 当理由单独作为答案出现时，同一个词就能承载它，前面不需要主句。

senses.title: With of before a noun
senses.definition: in the phrase because of, followed by a noun or noun phrase instead of a clause
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 because of，后面接名词或名词短语而非从句
senses.example: We stayed inside because of the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 由于大风，我们待在屋里。
senses.why: A clause needs a conjunction, but a bare noun needs a preposition, so of was added to carry the same reason.
senses.whyCN: 从句需要连词，而单独的名词需要介词，于是加上 of 来承载同样的原因。

intro.en: Because began as a two-word phrase, by cause, and the two parts fused into one conjunction.
intro.cn: because 最初是 by cause 这个两词短语，两部分后来粘合成了一个连词。

items.en: Latin causa meant a reason, a motive, or a legal case, and it is the source of cause.
items.cn: 拉丁语 causa 指原因、动机或案件，是 cause 的来源。

items.en: Old French cause carried the word into English with the meaning of a reason.
items.cn: 古法语 cause 把这个词带入英语，意为「原因」。

items.en: The phrase bi cause, meaning by the cause, was used to introduce a reason.
items.cn: 中古英语短语 bi cause 意为「凭这个原因」，用来引出一个理由。

items.en: The phrase was written as one word, and the spelling settled as because; the exact date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个短语后来写成一个词，拼写定为 because，确切年代不确定。

items.en: Because of was added later so that a bare noun could also follow the same reason word.
items.cn: because of 是后来加上的，好让单独的名词也能跟在同一个表示原因的词后面。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built from cause; the near-meaning group gathers other reason words that work differently in a sentence.
note.cn: 形近组收由 cause 构成的词；近义组收其他表示原因、但句中用法不同的词。

entries.definition: A reason for something, or to make something happen.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「原因；导致」，是 because 后半部分的来源。

entries.definition: A preposition phrase meaning as a result of.
entries.definitionCN: 介词短语，义为「由于」，后接名词。

entries.definition: Adjective meaning relating to cause and effect.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「因果的」，与 cause 同源。

entries.definition: A reason given to explain a fault; it looks similar but comes from a different Latin word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「借口；原谅」；拼写相近，但来自另一个拉丁词。

entries.definition: A conjunction giving a reason, but it also carries the sense of time from then on.
entries.definitionCN: 连词，也可引出理由，但还带有「自从那时」的时间意味。

entries.definition: A conjunction that can give a reason, with a more formal or written tone.
entries.definitionCN: 连词，也能引出理由，语气更正式、更书面。

entries.definition: An old conjunction meaning because, now mostly literary.
entries.definitionCN: 古老的连词，意为「因为」，现在多用于书面或文学语体。

entries.definition: A conjunction that introduces the result rather than the reason.
entries.definitionCN: 连词，引出的是结果而不是原因，方向与 because 相反。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real by cause origin and the fixed phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的 by cause 来源，以及这个词实际出现的固定搭配。

normal.en: Because was once by cause, so it literally means by the cause.
normal.cn: because 过去写作 by cause，字面意思是「凭这个原因」。

normal.en: Because introduces a clause, while because of introduces a noun.
normal.cn: because 引出从句，because of 引出名词。

normal.en: Just because is a phrase that refuses to give a real reason.
normal.cn: just because 是拒绝给出真正理由时的说法。

normal.en: A why question can be answered with because alone, without a main clause.
normal.cn: 回答 why 提问时可以只用一个 because，前面不加主句。

normal.en: Because and cause share the second half, so the reason is built into the word.
normal.cn: because 与 cause 共享后半部分，理由就写在这个词里。

abstract.en: Picture two dots joined by a line: the second dot exists only because of the first.
abstract.cn: 想象两个点被一条线连起来：后一个点的存在正是因为前一个点。

abstract.en: English separates the clause word and the noun word, so the same reason needs two tools.
abstract.cn: 英语把「接从句」和「接名词」分成两个词，所以同一个原因需要两件工具。

abstract.en: A reason is a bridge: it does not change the result, it only explains how the result arrived.
abstract.cn: 原因是座桥：它不改变结果，只说明结果是怎么来的。

examples.en: The match was cancelled because it rained.
examples.cn: 因为下雨，比赛被取消了。

examples.en: Why are you late? Because the bus broke down.
examples.cn: 你为什么迟到？因为公交车坏了。

examples.en: We stayed inside because of the wind.
examples.cn: 由于大风，我们待在屋里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「比靠兹」——比谁靠得住，就因为这个：因为

root: because 由中古英语短语 bi cause「凭这个原因」粘合而成。cause 经古法语 cause 来自拉丁语 causa「原因、案件」，因此 because 的字面义就是「凭这个原因」，后加 of 以便直接接名词。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of because all carry one reason: a reason clause, a standalone answer to why, and the because of form that takes a noun.
sensesIntro.cn: because 的三个义项都在承载同一个理由：接从句说明原因、单独作答 why，以及后接名词的 because of 形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two lines meet at a point, and the back line explains the front one.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条线在一点相接，后面那条解释了前面那条。

branches.en: THE CLAUSE: a full sentence of reason follows the conjunction.
branches.cn: 从句线：连词后面跟着一个完整的原因句。

branches.en: THE ANSWER: the same word stands alone when it replies to why.
branches.cn: 作答线：回答 why 时，同一个词可以单独站立。

branches.en: THE NOUN: because of lets a bare noun carry the reason.
branches.cn: 名词线：because of 让单独的名词也能承载原因。

branches.en: THE ROOT: cause sits inside the word, so the reason is never far away.
branches.cn: 词根线：cause 藏在这个词里，原因从不远离。

branches.en: THE ORDER: English puts the result first and the reason after, so the reason arrives last.
branches.cn: 语序线：英语先说结果后说理由，所以原因总是后到。

intro.en: Because is a fused phrase rather than a derived word, but its parts still show the reason image.
intro.cn: because 是粘合的短语而非派生词，但它的构件仍显出「原因」的意象。

latinIntro.en: Latin causa is recorded and reaches English through French as cause, the second half of the phrase.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 causa 有文献记录，经法语以 cause 进入英语，正是这个短语的后半。

items.example: It survives in the first half of because.
items.exampleCN: 它保留在 because 的前半部分。

items.example: The cause of the fire was clear.
He left because he was tired.

items.exampleCN: 它与 because 构成 because of。

items.example: It appears in the older spelling bi cause.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在旧拼写 bi cause 中。

items.example: The report looks at causal links.
items.exampleCN: 报告研究的是因果联系。
这项研究考察因果关系。
它与 because 构成 just because。

definition_zh: 变成；成为；变得；适合（某人）；发生（于）
definition_en: to start to be something, or to change into a state
core_image: 一棵小苗一天天长高，最后长成大树
scene: 天边云变厚，光线很快暗下来。The sky became dark very quickly.
sceneCN: 这里 become 是「变得」（第 1 个义项：进入某种状态）；句意为天色很快变暗了。

pos.zh: 动词：变成；成为；变得；适合

derivatives.zh: 由 become 加 -ing 构成，义为「合适的；相称的」
由否定前缀 un- 与 becoming 构成，义为「不相称的；不得体的」
基础词，义为「来」，become 由它加前缀构成

senses.title: To grow into a state
senses.definition: to start to have a quality, used before an adjective
senses.definitionCN: 开始具有某种性质，后接形容词
senses.example: The sky became dark very quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 天色很快变暗了。
senses.why: The Old English verb meant to come to a place; coming to a state is the same movement applied to qualities.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语动词本指「来到某处」，来到某种状态就是把同样的移动用在性质上。

senses.title: To turn into something
senses.definition: to come to be a particular thing or person, used before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 成为某种事物或人物，后接名词
senses.example: She became a doctor last year.
senses.exampleCN: 她去年成了医生。
senses.why: Arriving at a new identity is the same arrival, only the destination is a role instead of a place.
senses.whyCN: 到达一个新身份是同一种抵达，只是目的地变成了角色而不是地点。

senses.title: To suit someone
senses.definition: to look right on someone, or to be proper for them, in formal use
senses.definitionCN: 在某人身上好看，或与某人相称，属正式用法
senses.example: That blue coat becomes you.
senses.exampleCN: 那件蓝色外套很衬你。
senses.why: Something that comes well to a person fits them, and fitting grew out of the fitting of clothes.
senses.whyCN: 「合适地来到某人身上」就是与他相配，这个义项从衣服合身长出来。

senses.title: To happen to
senses.definition: in the phrase become of, to happen to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 become of，指某人或某物遭遇了什么
senses.example: What became of your old bike?
senses.exampleCN: 你那辆旧自行车后来怎么样了？
senses.why: The idea of coming to be extends to time: what a thing came to be tells what happened to it.
senses.whyCN: 「成为」的观念延伸到时间上：某物最终成了什么，就说明它遭遇了什么。

intro.en: Become is Old English becuman, made of be- plus cuman, to come.
intro.cn: become 是古英语 becuman，由前缀 be- 与 cuman「来」构成。

items.en: The Germanic verb meaning to come is the root of the second half.
items.cn: 表示「来」的日耳曼语动词是后半部分的词根。

items.en: Old English cuman meant to come or to arrive.
items.cn: 古英语 cuman 意为「来、到达」。

items.en: The prefixed verb becuman meant to come to, to arrive at, or to happen.
items.cn: 加前缀的动词 becuman 意为「来到、达到、发生」。

items.en: The sense shifted from arriving at a place to arriving at a state or an identity.
items.cn: 词义从「到达某地」转向「到达某种状态或身份」。

items.en: The phrase become of keeps the older sense of what something comes to.
items.cn: 短语 become of 保留了「某物最终如何」这一较古老的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and relatives of become; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs of change and of suitability.
note.cn: 形近组收 become 的形式与亲属词；近义组收表示变化与相称的其他动词。

entries.definition: The third person singular present form.
entries.definitionCN: becomes 是第三人称单数现在时形式。

entries.definition: The past tense form, using a different vowel.
entries.definitionCN: became 是过去式，元音发生变化。

entries.definition: The present participle, also an adjective meaning suitable.
entries.definitionCN: becoming 是现在分词，也作形容词，义为「合适的」。

entries.definition: The base verb meaning to move towards the speaker.
entries.definitionCN: come 是基础动词，义为「来、朝说话人移动」。

entries.definition: To change into something, often quickly or completely.
entries.definitionCN: turn 义为「变成」，常指快速或彻底的变化。

entries.definition: To become slowly through natural development.
entries.definitionCN: grow 义为「渐渐变得」，强调自然生长过程。

entries.definition: To become, in everyday speech, as in get tired.
entries.definitionCN: get 在口语中表示「变得」，如 get tired。

entries.definition: To look right on someone; the plain word for the third sense.
entries.definitionCN: suit 义为「适合、衬」，是第三个义项的普通说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real be- plus come structure and the irregular forms became and become.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的 be- 加 come 结构，以及 became、become 的不规则形式。

normal.en: Become is be- plus come, so becoming something means coming to it.
normal.cn: become 是 be- 加 come，所以成为某物就是「来到」它那里。

normal.en: The past tense is became, but the past participle stays become.
normal.cn: 过去式是 became，但过去分词仍是 become。

normal.en: Become plus an adjective gives a state, and become plus a noun gives an identity.
normal.cn: become 加形容词给的是状态，加名词给的是身份。

normal.en: Becoming as an adjective means suitable, because it becomes the person.
normal.cn: becoming 作形容词意为「合适的」，因为它「配得上」那个人。

normal.en: What became of it? asks what it came to in the end.
normal.cn: What became of it? 问的是它最后成了什么。

abstract.en: Picture a path: the traveller does not change, only the place he arrives at.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路：旅人没有变，变的只是他到达的地方。

abstract.en: A seed becoming a tree takes years, while a sky becoming dark takes minutes, and one word covers both.
abstract.cn: 种子长成大树要几年，天色变暗只要几分钟，同一个词把两者都装下了。

abstract.en: English lets arrival mean change, because arriving somewhere new is already a kind of becoming.
abstract.cn: 英语让「到达」表示「变化」，因为抵达一个新地方本身就已经是一种成为。

examples.en: The sky became dark very quickly.
examples.cn: 天色很快变暗了。

examples.en: She became a doctor last year.
examples.cn: 她去年成了医生。

examples.en: What became of your old bike?
examples.cn: 你那辆旧自行车后来怎么样了？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必看」——想成为高手，必看这本手册：成为

root: become 来自古英语 becuman，由前缀 be- 与 cuman「来」构成，cuman 源于日耳曼语中表示「来」的动词。词义由「到达某处」引申为「到达某种状态或身份」，故有「变得、成为」；成为 of 短语保留「最终如何」的旧义。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of become all come from arriving: arriving at a quality, at an identity, at a good fit, and at a final outcome.
sensesIntro.cn: become 的四个义项都来自「抵达」：抵达某种性质、抵达某个身份、抵达合身相称，以及抵达最终结局。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small shoot grows taller each week until it stands as a tree.
core.cn: 核心意象：一棵小苗每周都长高一点，最后站成一棵树。

branches.en: THE STATE: coming to an adjective means entering that condition.
branches.cn: 状态线：来到一个形容词上，就是进入那种状况。

branches.en: THE IDENTITY: coming to a noun means taking that role.
branches.cn: 身份线：来到一个名词上，就是取得那个角色。

branches.en: THE FIT: clothes that come well to a person suit them.
branches.cn: 合身线：合适地「来到」某人身上的衣服就衬他。

branches.en: THE OUTCOME: what a thing came to tells what happened to it.
branches.cn: 结局线：某物最终来到什么样子，就说明它遭遇了什么。

branches.en: THE CHANGE: the traveller stays the same, only the arrival point moves.
branches.cn: 变化线：旅人本身不变，移动的只是抵达之处。

intro.en: Become is a prefixed strong verb, and the prefix be- is no longer a separate word in English.
intro.cn: become 是加前缀的强变化动词，前缀 be- 在现代英语中已不能独立成词。

latinIntro.en: The whole verb is Germanic, so no Latin cognate is recorded and the list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 整个动词属日耳曼语，没有记录在案的拉丁同族词，因此列表留空。

items.exampleCN: 它与 come 构成 become。
它与 become 构成 become of。
它与 become 构成 become aware of。

definition_zh: 床；就寝；花坛；河床；岩层
definition_en: a piece of furniture for sleeping on, or a flat layer of ground
core_image: 一张铺好被褥的床，被子整整齐齐叠在一端
scene: 早晨起床后，她把被子叠好，铺平了床面。She made her bed before breakfast.
sceneCN: 这里 bed 是「床」（第 1 个义项：供睡觉的家具）；句意为早饭前她整理好了床铺。

pos.zh: 名词：床；就寝；花坛；河床；岩层

derivatives.zh: 由 bed 与 room 组合而成，义为「卧室」
由 bed 与 time 组合而成，义为「就寝时间」
由 bed 与 side 组合而成，义为「床边」
由 flower 与 bed 组合而成，义为「花坛」

senses.title: Furniture for sleeping
senses.definition: a piece of furniture with a mattress, used for sleeping
senses.definitionCN: 带床垫、供睡觉的家具
senses.example: She made her bed before breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 早饭前她整理好了床铺。
senses.why: The Old English word named the sleeping place itself, so the furniture is the first and central sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语词指睡觉之处本身，所以家具义是第一义，也是中心义。

senses.title: Sleep or rest
senses.definition: used in phrases such as go to bed to mean sleep or rest at night
senses.definitionCN: 用于 go to bed 等短语，指夜里睡觉或休息
senses.example: The children go to bed at nine.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们九点上床睡觉。
senses.why: The place of sleeping stands for the activity of sleeping, a common shift from object to action.
senses.whyCN: 睡觉的地方代替了睡觉这件事，这是从器物到动作的常见转移。

senses.title: A planted area
senses.definition: a flat area of ground where flowers or plants are grown
senses.definitionCN: 种植花卉或植物的平整地块
senses.example: They planted roses in a bed by the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在墙边的花坛里种了玫瑰。
senses.why: A prepared patch of soil is a soft flat surface like a mattress, so gardeners borrowed the same word.
senses.whyCN: 整好的地块像床垫一样松软平整，于是园艺用上了同一个词。

senses.title: The bottom of a river
senses.definition: the ground at the bottom of a river, lake, or sea
senses.definitionCN: 河、湖或海的底部地面
senses.example: The river bed was dry in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天河床干涸了。
senses.why: The lowest layer where things settle is a bed in the same flat, supporting way.
senses.whyCN: 东西沉落的最底层，同样平整而承托，所以也叫 bed。

senses.title: A layer of rock
senses.definition: a flat layer of rock or other material lying under the ground
senses.definitionCN: 地面之下平铺的一层岩石或其他物质
senses.example: Workers found a bed of clay under the field.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们在田地下发现了一层黏土。
senses.why: Geology sees each flat layer as a bed that later layers lie upon.
senses.whyCN: 地质学把每一层平整的岩层看作一张「床」，后来的层都躺在它上面。

intro.en: Bed is Old English bedd, and it is generally linked to a root meaning to dig, because early beds were hollows.
intro.cn: bed 是古英语 bedd，一般认为与表示「挖掘」的词根有关，因为早期床铺是挖出的浅坑。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to dig or to pierce is generally thought to lie behind the word.
items.cn: 一般认为一个可重构、意为「挖掘、穿透」的词根是它的远源。

items.en: The Germanic form named a sleeping place made of leaves or straw.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形式指用树叶或稻草铺成的睡处。

items.en: Old English bedd named the sleeping place and later the furniture.
items.cn: 古英语 bedd 指睡处，后来指家具。

items.en: The word extended to flat patches of ground, such as a flower bed.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到平整的地块，如花坛。

items.en: Geology and geography use bed for river bottoms and flat rock layers.
items.cn: 地质学与地理学用 bed 指河底与平整的岩层。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds built on bed; the near-meaning group gathers sleeping furniture and flat layers.
note.cn: 形近组收由 bed 构成的复合词；近义组收睡眠家具与平整层状物。

entries.definition: A room used for sleeping.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「卧室」，由 bed 与 room 组合而成。

entries.definition: The usual hour for going to bed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「就寝时间」，由 bed 与 time 组合而成。

entries.definition: The area beside a bed, especially in a hospital.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「床边」，尤指病床旁，由 bed 与 side 组合而成。

entries.definition: A patch of ground planted with flowers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「花坛」，由 flower 与 bed 组合而成。

entries.definition: The soft pad that lies on a bed frame.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「床垫」，铺在床架上的软垫。

entries.definition: A small bed with high sides, for a baby; British use.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「婴儿床」，四周有高边，英式用法。

entries.definition: A flat thickness of material lying over another; close to the rock sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「层」，与「岩层」义接近。

entries.definition: A small area of ground, often planted; it fits the flower sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小块地」，常用于种植，对应「花坛」义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real dig-root story, the compounds, and the fixed phrases with bed.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的「挖掘」词根故事、复合词，以及 bed 的固定搭配。

normal.en: Early beds were hollows dug in the ground, which is why the root is linked to digging.
normal.cn: 早期的床是地上挖出的浅坑，所以词根与「挖掘」有关。

normal.en: Go to bed uses bed for sleep itself, not for the furniture.
normal.cn: go to bed 里的 bed 指睡觉这件事，而不是家具。

normal.en: A flower bed is a flat prepared patch, soft and level like a mattress.
normal.cn: 花坛是整平的软地块，像床垫一样平整。

normal.en: River bed and rock bed keep the idea of a flat layer underneath.
normal.cn: 河床与岩层都保留了「下面一层平整之物」的意思。

normal.en: Bedside is where someone sits to talk to a person who is ill.
normal.cn: bedside 是人坐着与病人说话的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a hollow filled with leaves: the first bed was less furniture than a shaped patch of ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一个铺满树叶的浅坑：最初的床更像一块被整出的地，而不是家具。

abstract.en: The same flatness runs from mattress to flower bed to rock bed, one shape under many names.
abstract.cn: 同样的平铺从床垫延伸到花坛再到岩层，一个形状撑起许多名字。

abstract.en: A bed is where a body stops moving, and the word quietly keeps that stillness in every other sense.
abstract.cn: 床是身体停止移动的地方，这个词在其余义项里也悄悄保留着那份静止。

examples.en: She made her bed before breakfast.
examples.cn: 早饭前她整理好了床铺。

examples.en: The children go to bed at nine.
examples.cn: 孩子们九点上床睡觉。

examples.en: The river bed was dry in summer.
examples.cn: 夏天河床干涸了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「贝德」——贝德每天把被子叠成方块：床

root: bed 来自古英语 bedd，源于日耳曼语 bathjam，一般认为可上溯到原始印欧语中意为「挖掘」的重构词根，因早期床铺是挖出的浅坑。词义由睡处扩展到家具，再由「平整铺开」扩展到花坛、河床与岩层。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of bed spread from one flat sleeping place: the furniture, the act of sleeping, a planted patch, a river bottom, and a rock layer.
sensesIntro.cn: bed 的五个义项都从一个平整的睡处扩展：家具、睡觉这件事、种植地块、河底，以及岩层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bed with folded blankets sits level against the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张被子叠好的床平贴着墙放着。

branches.en: THE FURNITURE: the sleeping place becomes the object bought and made up.
branches.cn: 家具线：睡处变成了可以购买和整理的物件。

branches.en: THE SLEEP: the place stands for the activity of resting there.
branches.cn: 睡觉线：那处地方代表了在那里休息这件事。

branches.en: THE PLOT: a level patch of soil takes the same flat word.
branches.cn: 地块线：平整的一块土沿用同一个「平铺」的词。

branches.en: THE BOTTOM: whatever settles at the lowest point lies in a bed.
branches.cn: 底层线：沉在最低处的东西都躺在一张「床」上。

branches.en: THE LAYER: geology sees rock as flat beds stacked over each other.
branches.cn: 层状线：地质学把岩石看作彼此叠压的平整层。

intro.en: Bed is a short Germanic root whose family grows mainly by compounding.
intro.cn: bed 是简短的日耳曼语词根，其词族主要靠复合构词生长。

latinIntro.en: No Latin cognate is recorded for this Germanic root, so the list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个日耳曼语词根没有记录在案的拉丁同族词，因此列表留空。

definition_zh: 卧室；卧室用的（作定语）
definition_en: a room used for sleeping, especially in a house
core_image: 一间小屋，床靠着窗，窗帘半开着
scene: 新房子很大，她挑了一间有落地窗的屋子当自己的房间。Her bedroom has a big window and a soft bed.
sceneCN: 这里 bedroom 是「卧室」（第 1 个义项：供睡觉的房间）；句意为她的卧室有一扇大窗和一张软床。

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「床」，是 bedroom 的前半部分
基础词，义为「房间」，是 bedroom 的后半部分
由 bedroom 加 -ed 构成，用于复合表达如 four-bedroomed，义为「有若干卧室的」

senses.title: A room for sleeping
senses.definition: a room in a house used for sleeping
senses.definitionCN: 房子里供睡觉的房间
senses.example: Her bedroom has a big window and a soft bed.
senses.exampleCN: 她的卧室有一扇大窗和一张软床。
senses.why: The compound simply joins bed and room, so its first sense is the room that holds the bed.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词只是把 bed 与 room 合在一起，第一义就是放床的那间房。

senses.title: Used before another noun
senses.definition: placed before another noun to show that the thing belongs to or is used in a bedroom
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，表示该物属于卧室或供卧室使用
senses.example: He closed the bedroom door quietly.
senses.exampleCN: 他轻轻关上了卧室的门。
senses.why: Once the room is a familiar unit, its name can label the things inside and around it.
senses.whyCN: 当这间房成为熟悉的单位，它的名字就能给屋内的东西贴标签。

senses.title: Counting rooms in a home
senses.definition: used in compounds such as two-bedroom to count the sleeping rooms of a home
senses.definitionCN: 用于 two-bedroom 这类复合词，统计住所中卧室的数量
senses.example: They rent a two-bedroom flat near the school.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在学校附近租了一套两居室。
senses.why: Because a home is measured by its sleeping rooms, the word became a counting unit in housing descriptions.
senses.whyCN: 因为住房常按卧室数量来衡量，这个词在描述住房时就成了计数单位。

intro.en: Bedroom is a straightforward English compound of bed and room, recorded from the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: bedroom 是 bed 与 room 直接的英语复合词，十七世纪已有记录。

items.en: Bed goes back to the Old English word for a sleeping place.
items.cn: bed 可追溯到古英语中表示睡处的词。

items.en: Room goes back to Old English rum, meaning space or an open area.
items.cn: room 可追溯到古英语 rum，意为「空间、开阔处」。

items.en: By the Middle Ages room meant a separate chamber inside a building.
items.cn: 到中世纪时，room 已指建筑内部独立的房间。

items.en: Bedroom appears in the seventeenth century, naming the chamber for sleeping.
items.cn: bedroom 于十七世纪出现，指供睡觉的房间。

items.en: Later usage counts bedrooms, as in a two-bedroom flat.
items.cn: 后来的用法按卧室计数，如 a two-bedroom flat。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other room compounds; the near-meaning group gathers words for rooms and for sleeping places.
note.cn: 形近组收其他「房间」复合词；近义组收表示房间与睡处的词。

entries.definition: A room for washing or a room with a toilet.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「浴室、洗手间」，构词方式相同。

entries.definition: A room where a class is taught.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「教室」，构词方式相同。

entries.definition: The furniture for sleeping, the first half of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「床」，是复合词的前半部分。

entries.definition: A separate space inside a building, the second half.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「房间」，是复合词的后半部分。

entries.definition: A set of rooms to live in, described by how many bedrooms it has.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「公寓」，常按卧室数量描述，英式用法。

entries.definition: A large room or building where many people sleep, as at a school.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宿舍」，供多人同住，常见于学校。

entries.definition: A small bed with high sides for a baby; a place, not a room.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「婴儿床」，指家具而不是房间。

entries.definition: A large room or passage in a building; larger than a bedroom.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大厅、走廊」，比卧室更大。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two real halves and the parallel room words built the same way.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用两个真实的组成部分，以及用同样方式造出的平行「房间」词。

normal.en: Bed plus room is literal, just like bath plus room and class plus room.
normal.cn: bed 加 room 完全字面，就像 bath 加 room、class 加 room 一样。

normal.en: A two-bedroom flat is counted by its sleeping rooms, not by all its rooms.
normal.cn: two-bedroom flat 按睡觉的房间计数，而不是按所有房间。

normal.en: Bedroom window and bedroom door show the attributive use in daily speech.
normal.cn: bedroom window 与 bedroom door 体现日常口语中的定语用法。

normal.en: A spare bedroom is one nobody usually sleeps in.
normal.cn: spare bedroom 是平时没人睡的那间卧室。

normal.en: Hotel rooms are not called bedrooms, so the word points to a home.
normal.cn: 旅馆房间不叫 bedroom，所以这个词指向住宅。

abstract.en: Picture a small room with one bed and one window: the whole word is that picture.
abstract.cn: 想象一间小屋，一张床、一扇窗：整个词就是这幅画。

abstract.en: English names rooms by what happens in them, so the bed gives the room its name.
abstract.cn: 英语按房间里发生的事给房间命名，所以床给了这间房名字。

abstract.en: A bedroom is the one room where a person is alone and still, which is why the word feels private.
abstract.cn: 卧室是人独处且静止的那间房，所以这个词带着私密感。

examples.en: Her bedroom has a big window and a soft bed.
examples.cn: 她的卧室有一扇大窗和一张软床。

examples.en: He closed the bedroom door quietly.
examples.cn: 他轻轻关上了卧室的门。

examples.en: They rent a two-bedroom flat near the school.
examples.cn: 他们在学校附近租了一套两居室。

root: bedroom 是 bed 与 room 的英语复合词。bed 来自古英语 bedd「睡处」，一般认为与「挖掘」词根有关；room 来自古英语 rum「空间」，后指建筑内的独立房间。十七世纪起用 bedroom 指卧室，现代又用它统计住房的卧室数量。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of bedroom go from the room itself, to its attributive use before other nouns, to its role as a counting unit for homes.
sensesIntro.cn: bedroom 的三个义项从房间本身，到放在其他名词前的定语用法，再到作为住房计数单位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one bed, one window, and a door that closes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张床、一扇窗，还有一扇能关上的门。

branches.en: THE ROOM: bed plus room simply names the chamber that holds the bed.
branches.cn: 房间线：bed 加 room 就是放床的那间屋子。

branches.en: THE ATTRIBUTE: the room's name labels its window, door, and slippers.
branches.cn: 定语线：房间的名字给它的窗、门、拖鞋贴标签。

branches.en: THE COUNT: homes are measured by how many sleeping rooms they have.
branches.cn: 计数线：住房按有几间睡房来衡量。

branches.en: THE PRIVACY: a bedroom is where the door can shut on the world.
branches.cn: 私密线：卧室是能把世界关在门外的地方。

branches.en: THE PATTERN: bath, class and bed all name rooms the same way.
branches.cn: 构词线：bath、class 与 bed 用同样方式给房间命名。

intro.en: Bedroom is one of the many English compounds that name a room by its purpose.
intro.cn: bedroom 是英语中按用途命名房间的众多复合词之一。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are Germanic, so no Latin cognate is recorded and the list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都属日耳曼语，没有记录在案的拉丁同族词，因此列表留空。

definition_zh: 蜜蜂；蜂类昆虫；拼字比赛；忙碌的人
definition_en: a flying insect that collects nectar and makes honey, also used in a few fixed phrases
core_image: 一只在花丛间采蜜的蜂，后腿上挂着两团黄花粉
scene: 花园里，一只蜜蜂围着向日葵转了两圈，然后飞回蜂巢。A bee landed on the yellow flower and began to collect pollen.
sceneCN: 这里 bee 是「蜜蜂」（第 1 个义项：采蜜的蜂类昆虫）；句意为一只蜜蜂落在黄花上，开始采集花粉。

pos.zh: 名词：蜜蜂；蜂类；拼字比赛

derivatives.zh: 由 bee 与 hive 组合而成，义为「蜂箱；蜂巢」
由 bee 与 keeper 组合而成，义为「养蜂人」
由 bee 与 wax 组合而成，义为「蜂蜡」

senses.title: The honey-making insect
senses.definition: a flying insect with four wings that collects nectar from flowers and makes honey
senses.definitionCN: 一种有四片翅膀、从花中采蜜并酿蜜的飞虫
senses.example: A bee landed on the yellow flower.
senses.exampleCN: 一只蜜蜂落在黄花上。
senses.why: Old English beo named this insect, and every Germanic sister language points at the same buzzing creature, so the insect is the oldest and strongest sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 beo 就指这种昆虫，日耳曼语各亲属语言都指同一只会嗡嗡叫的虫子，所以「蜜蜂」是最古老也最稳固的义项。

senses.title: Bees as a group
senses.definition: any of a large group of related stinging insects, whether or not they make honey
senses.definitionCN: 一大类有近缘关系、会蜇人的昆虫，无论是否酿蜜
senses.example: Bees and wasps look alike to many people.
senses.exampleCN: 在很多人眼里，蜜蜂和黄蜂长得差不多。
senses.why: Because the common bee and its relatives share a body plan and a sting, the name spread from the honey bee to the whole group.
senses.whyCN: 因为常见的蜜蜂与近亲共享同一体型和一根蜇针，这个名字就从蜜蜂扩展到了整类昆虫。

senses.title: A spelling bee
senses.definition: a contest in which people, especially children, spell words aloud and are eliminated when they miss
senses.definitionCN: 一种比赛，参加者尤其多为儿童，轮流口头拼写单词，拼错即被淘汰
senses.example: She won the school spelling bee.
senses.exampleCN: 她在学校的拼字比赛中获胜。
senses.why: An old bee meant a gathering of neighbours to work together, and spelling bee kept the gathering sense while narrowing it to a contest in spelling.
senses.whyCN: 旧时的 bee 指邻里聚在一起互相帮工，spelling bee 保留了「聚会」的意思，只把内容收窄成拼写竞赛。

senses.title: A busy person
senses.definition: used in the phrase a busy bee for someone who is always active and working
senses.definitionCN: 用在 a busy bee 这一说法中，指总是忙忙碌碌做事的人
senses.example: My aunt is a busy bee in the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 我姨妈在厨房里忙个不停。
senses.why: A bee never stops moving from flower to flower, so the insect became a natural picture for a person who cannot sit still.
senses.whyCN: 蜜蜂从一朵花飞到另一朵花，从不停歇，于是这只昆虫自然成了形容坐不住的人的画面。

intro.en: Bee is an old Germanic insect name; the gathering sense is a later English development.
intro.cn: bee 是古老的日耳曼语昆虫名；「聚会」义是后来在英语里发展出来的。

items.en: Old English beo named the honey-making insect, and the word was already short and common.
items.cn: 古英语 beo 指酿蜜的昆虫，这个词当时已很短、很常用。

items.en: Dutch bij and German Biene are close relatives, and all go back to one Germanic name for the insect.
items.cn: 荷兰语 bij 与德语 Biene 是近亲，都可追溯到同一个日耳曼语昆虫名。

items.en: The spelling settled as bee, while the meaning stayed firmly on the insect.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 bee，词义则稳定留在这种昆虫上。

items.en: In early modern English a bee could also mean a gathering of neighbours working together, as in a husking bee.
items.cn: 在近代早期英语里，bee 还可以指邻里聚在一起干活，例如剥玉米的聚会 husking bee。

items.en: That gathering sense now survives mainly in spelling bee, while the insect remains the everyday meaning.
items.cn: 那个「聚会」义如今主要保留在 spelling bee 里，而昆虫义仍是日常用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects short words built on the same sounds; the near-meaning group collects other stinging insects.
note.cn: 形近组收同一批读音很短的词；近义组收其他会蜇人的昆虫。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to exist or to have a quality; it sounds exactly like bee.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「是、存在」，读音与 bee 完全相同。

entries.definition: The meat of cattle; it begins with the same long vowel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「牛肉」，以同一个长元音开头。

entries.definition: A kind of insect with hard wing cases; another insect word with the same first sound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「甲虫」，是另一个以同一音开头的昆虫词。

entries.definition: The plural of bee, with a voiced ending.
entries.definitionCN: bee 的复数形式，词尾读作浊音。

entries.definition: A thin-bodied stinging insect that does not make honey.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「黄蜂」，体型细长、会蜇人但不酿蜜。

entries.definition: A large wasp with a painful sting.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大黄蜂」，体型大、蜇人很痛。

entries.definition: The specific bee kept for honey; it names the first sense more exactly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蜜蜂」，专指用来产蜜的蜂，比 bee 更精确。

entries.definition: A small social insect that lives in colonies, like the bee.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蚂蚁」，与蜜蜂一样是群居昆虫。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded Germanic family, the real compounds, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的日耳曼语词族、真实复合词和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Old English beo meant this insect, and Dutch bij and German Biene still do.
normal.cn: 古英语 beo 就指这种昆虫，荷兰语 bij 和德语 Biene 至今仍如此。

normal.en: Picture the pollen baskets on the back legs: that is the honey-making bee.
normal.cn: 想象后腿上的花粉篮，那就是酿蜜的蜜蜂。

normal.en: The bee in spelling bee is not an insect but an old word for a gathering.
normal.cn: spelling bee 里的 bee 不是虫子，而是旧时表示「聚会」的词。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with queen, worker, sting and hive.
normal.cn: 它常与 queen、worker、sting、hive 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-e-e: three letters with two e's side by side, like two bees on a flower.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-e-e，三个字母里两个 e 并排，像花上并排的两只蜂。

abstract.en: See a bee lift off, dropping a little pollen behind it: that is the act of collecting.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蜂起飞，身后洒下一点花粉，那就是「采集」的动作。

abstract.en: Lay the picture of a gathering over the insect picture, and spelling bee follows naturally.
abstract.cn: 把「聚在一起」的画面叠到昆虫画面上，拼字比赛就顺理成章。

abstract.en: Say the long vowel first, then let the flower bring the insect back.
abstract.cn: 先读出那个长元音，再让花的画面把昆虫带回来。

examples.cn: 一只蜜蜂落在黄花上。

root: bee 来自古英语 beo，是日耳曼语里对酿蜜蜂的古老称呼，荷兰语 bij 与德语 Biene 都与它同源。近代英语里 bee 还指邻里聚在一起干活的聚会，这一用法今天主要保存在 spelling bee 中。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of bee grow from one picture: a small insect that never stops moving from flower to flower.
sensesIntro.cn: bee 的四个义项都从同一幅画面生长出来：一只从一朵花飞向另一朵花、从不停歇的小虫。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bee carrying two balls of pollen on its back legs
core.cn: 核心意象：一只后腿挂着两团花粉的蜜蜂

branches.en: THE INSECT: the honey-making bee is the sense every other use rests on.
branches.cn: 昆虫线：酿蜜的蜜蜂是其他用法所依靠的义项。

branches.en: THE GROUP: wasps and other relatives widen the name to a whole family of stinging insects.
branches.cn: 同类线：黄蜂等近亲把这个名字扩展到一整类会蜇人的昆虫。

branches.en: THE GATHERING: the old sense of neighbours meeting survives inside spelling bee.
branches.cn: 聚会线：邻里相聚的旧义保存在拼字比赛这个词组里。

branches.en: THE WORKER: a bee never rests, so the picture also names a busy person.
branches.cn: 勤劳线：蜜蜂从不停歇，于是这幅画也用来指忙碌的人。

branches.en: THE SPREAD: one old word for a gathering and one word for an insect ended up in the same three letters.
branches.cn: 合流线：一个表示聚会的旧词和一个表示昆虫的词，最后落在同样的三个字母上。

intro.en: Bee is a base noun; the listed parts are real compounds and inflections built on it.
intro.cn: bee 是基础名词，下面列出的是由它构成的真实复合词与屈折形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin apis is recorded for the bee, but English took the word from Germanic, not from Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语确有 apis 表示蜜蜂，但英语这个词来自日耳曼语，并非借自拉丁语。

definition_zh: 在……之前；在……面前；以前；当着……的面
definition_en: earlier than a time or event, or in front of someone or something
core_image: 一条时间线上，手指落在当前这一刻的左边
scene: 早晨的教室里，铃声还没响，几个学生已经在门口等着。The bell rings before the teacher arrives.
sceneCN: 这里 before 是「在……之前」（第 1 个义项：时间上早于某事）；句意为老师到来之前铃就响了。

derivatives.zh: 由 before 与 hand 组合而成，义为「事先；预先」
同源成分，义为「前面的；前部的」，见于 forehead、forecast 等词

senses.title: Earlier than a time
senses.definition: earlier than a particular time, event, or action
senses.definitionCN: 早于某个具体时间、事件或动作
senses.example: Finish your homework before dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭前把作业做完。
senses.why: Old English beforan is be-, meaning at or by, plus foran, meaning in front; on a line of time the earlier point is the one further in front, so before marks earlier time.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 beforan 由 be-「在」加 foran「在前面」构成；在时间线更前面的点就是更早的点，所以 before 标记较早的时间。

senses.title: In front of a place
senses.definition: in front of a place, object, or person, especially in a position facing it
senses.definitionCN: 在某地、某物或某人前方，尤指面对它的位置
senses.example: She stood before the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她站在门前。
senses.why: The second element foran meant literally in front, so the place sense is the one closest to the original picture of standing ahead of something.
senses.whyCN: 后一半 foran 本义就是「在前面」，所以位置义最接近「站在某物前方」这个最初的画面。

senses.title: At an earlier time, standing alone
senses.definition: used as an adverb, without an object, for a time earlier than now
senses.definitionCN: 作副词单独使用，不带宾语，指早于现在的时间
senses.example: I have seen this film before.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影我以前看过。
senses.why: When the object is dropped, the word still keeps the same earlier point on the line, but it now means earlier than now rather than earlier than a named event.
senses.whyCN: 去掉宾语后，这个词仍落在时间线的同一个较前位置，只是变成「早于现在」，而不是「早于某个具体事件」。

senses.title: In the presence of people
senses.definition: in the presence of a person or group, so that they see or hear what happens
senses.definitionCN: 在某个人或一群人面前，使他们看到或听到所发生的事
senses.example: He said it before the whole class.
senses.exampleCN: 他当着全班的面说了这话。
senses.why: From standing in front of a place, the word moved to standing in front of people, and that is exactly the sense of doing something in their presence.
senses.whyCN: 从「站在某地前面」转到「站在人前面」，这正是「在众人面前做某事」的意思。

intro.en: Before is a fused Germanic compound whose two halves both meant in front.
intro.cn: before 是粘合的日耳曼语复合词，两半都带「在前面」的意思。

items.en: Old English beforan joined be-, meaning by or at, with foran, meaning in front.
items.cn: 古英语 beforan 由 be-「在、靠」加 foran「在前面」组成。

items.en: Foran belongs to a Germanic root for in front, which also gives Dutch voor and German vor.
items.cn: foran 属于日耳曼语中表示「在前面」的词根，荷兰语 voor 与德语 vor 也来自这里。

items.en: The two parts merged into a single word and served for both place and time.
items.cn: 两部分合并成一个词，同时用于位置和时间。

items.en: Because the front position is also the earlier position in a line, before came to mark earlier time more and more.
items.cn: 因为在一条线上靠前的位置也就是较早的位置，before 越来越多地用来标记更早的时间。

items.en: Today it works as preposition, conjunction and adverb, and the time sense is by far the most common.
items.cn: 今天它可作介词、连词和副词，其中时间义最常用。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words sharing the same opening or ending sounds; the near-meaning group collects words that also place one thing ahead of another.
note.cn: 形近组收开头或结尾读音相同的词；近义组收同样表示「一物在另一物之前」的词。

entries.definition: The verb of existence, which opens with the same two letters.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「是、存在」，开头两个字母与 before 相同。

entries.definition: An adjective for the front part, from the same old element.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「前面的」，来自同一个古老成分。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in advance, built from before plus hand.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「事先」，由 before 加 hand 构成。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to happen to someone, with a similar opening sound.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「降临到某人身上」，开头读音相近。

entries.definition: At a time before another time; it matches the time sense closely.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或形容词，义为「更早地」，与时间义最接近。

entries.definition: Coming before in time or order; more formal than before.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「先前的、优先的」，比 before 更正式。

entries.definition: In front of or earlier than something, matching both the place and time senses.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「在……前面、早于」，同时对应位置义与时间义。

entries.definition: Later than something; the direct opposite of the first sense.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……之后」，是第一个义项的直接反义。

normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的构件、日耳曼语亲属词和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Be- means at or by, and foran means in front: together they say at the front, which is earlier.
normal.cn: be- 表示「在、靠」，foran 表示「在前面」，合起来就是「在更前的位置」，也就是更早。

normal.en: Dutch voor and German vor are cousins and also mean in front.
normal.cn: 荷兰语 voor 与德语 vor 是它的表亲，也都表示「在前面」。

normal.en: Before and after are a pair: one points ahead, the other points behind.
normal.cn: before 与 after 是一对：一个指向前，一个指向后。

normal.en: It commonly appears in before long, the day before and before breakfast.
normal.cn: 它常出现在 before long、the day before、before breakfast 这些搭配里。

normal.en: Spell be plus fore: the two old parts are still visible inside the word.
normal.cn: 拼写是 be 加 fore：两个古老成分在词里仍看得见。

abstract.en: Draw a line of time and put your finger left of the present mark: that is before.
abstract.cn: 画一条时间线，把手指放在当前这一刻的左边，那就是 before。

abstract.en: Lay the picture of standing at a door over the picture of dinner not yet begun: front and earlier are the same picture.
abstract.cn: 把「站在门前」和「晚饭还没开始」叠在一起：前方与更早是同一幅画。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud, then let the line of time bring the meaning of earlier back.
abstract.cn: 先把词读出声，再让时间线把「更早」的意思带回来。

examples.cn: 晚饭前把作业做完。

examples.cn: 这部电影我以前看过。

examples.cn: 她站在门前。

root: before 来自古英语 beforan，由 be-「在、靠」与 foran「在前面」合成。因为队伍里靠前的位置也是较早的位置，这个词从空间上的「在前面」自然扩展到时间上的「更早」，今天最常用的正是时间义。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of before come from one picture: a point further ahead on a line, whether that line is space or time.
sensesIntro.cn: before 的四个义项都出自同一幅画面：一条线上更靠前的点，无论这条线是空间还是时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger placed to the left of the present point on a line
core.cn: 核心意象：手指落在一条线上当前点的左边

branches.en: THE EARLIER TIME: the front of a line becomes the earlier part of a day.
branches.cn: 先时线：一条线的前端变成一天中较早的那段。

branches.en: THE FRONT PLACE: the same word still means standing ahead of a door or a wall.
branches.cn: 前方线：同一个词仍表示站在门或墙的前面。

branches.en: THE BARE FORM: with no object, the word simply means earlier than now.
branches.cn: 独用线：不带宾语时，这个词就只表示早于现在。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: standing in front of a group turns into doing something in their presence.
branches.cn: 人前线：站在一群人前面，转成在众人面前做某事。

branches.en: THE SPLIT: place and time share one origin, and English lets the same form serve both.
branches.cn: 分用线：位置与时间共用一个来源，英语让同一个形式同时承担两者。

intro.en: Before is a fused compound, so its parts are Old English elements rather than productive affixes.
intro.cn: before 是粘合的复合词，所以它的构件是古英语成分，而非能产的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin has its own words for before, ante and prae, which are listed as parallels rather than as sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语有自己的「在……之前」用词 ante 与 prae，此处作为平行词列出，而非来源。

definition_zh: 开始；着手；起始于；起初是
definition_en: to start doing something, or to start to happen or exist
core_image: 起跑线上，第一只脚刚刚踏出去
scene: 操场上，体育老师吹响哨子，学生们同时从起跑线出发。The race begins when the whistle blows.
sceneCN: 这里 begin 是「开始」（第 1 个义项：某事开始发生）；句意为哨声一响，比赛就开始了。

pos.zh: 动词：开始；着手；起始于；起初是

derivatives.zh: 由 begin 加 -ing 构成，义为「开始；开端」
由 begin 加 -er 构成，义为「初学者；新手」

senses.title: To start doing something
senses.definition: to take the first step in an action, often followed by to do or doing
senses.definitionCN: 在某项行动中迈出第一步，后面常接 to do 或 doing
senses.example: She began to read the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 她开始读那封信。
senses.why: Old English beginnan joined be-, which sets about, with ginnan, to begin, so the verb literally means to set about an action.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 beginnan 由表「着手」的 be- 与表「开始」的 ginnan 组成，所以这个动词字面就是「着手做一件事」。

senses.title: For an event to start
senses.definition: for an event, period, or process to start, with no person doing the action
senses.definitionCN: 指事件、时段或过程自己开始，没有人去执行动作
senses.example: The film begins at seven.
senses.exampleCN: 电影七点开始。
senses.why: When nothing is being begun, the same verb keeps the first-step image but the subject is the event itself, so begin means simply to start happening.
senses.whyCN: 当没有谁去「开始」什么时，这个动词保留「第一步」的画面，但主语变成了事件本身，于是 begin 就只表示「开始发生」。

senses.title: To have something as a starting point
senses.definition: to start with a particular thing, place, or detail, often in begin with
senses.definitionCN: 以某事物、某处或某细节为开端，常用于 begin with 结构
senses.example: The story begins with a letter.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事以一封信开头。
senses.why: A first step needs a point to step from, and begin with names exactly that point, so the verb can mean to take something as the starting place.
senses.whyCN: 第一步总得有个落脚点，begin with 正是把这个落脚点点明，于是动词可以表示「以某物为起点」。

senses.title: To be at first
senses.definition: to exist at first in a particular form, before later changing
senses.definitionCN: 最初以某种形态存在，之后再发生变化
senses.example: The club began as a small reading group.
senses.exampleCN: 这个俱乐部起初只是一个小读书会。
senses.why: Push the first step back to the very earliest stage and it describes what something was at its start, which is the sense of beginning as something.
senses.whyCN: 把「第一步」一直往前推到最早的阶段，就变成描述某物开头时的样子，这就是「起初是某种事物」的义项。

intro.en: Begin is an old English compound verb that kept an irregular past tense.
intro.cn: begin 是古老的英语复合动词，保留了不规则的过去式。

items.en: Old English beginnan meant to start or to attempt, and it was already a compound verb.
items.cn: 古英语 beginnan 意为「开始、着手尝试」，当时已是复合动词。

items.en: The first element be- added the idea of setting about or going at something.
items.cn: 第一个成分 be- 增添了「着手、对着某物去」的意思。

items.en: The second element ginnan meant to begin, and it now survives only inside this verb and its forms.
items.cn: 第二个成分 ginnan 意为「开始」，今天只存活在这个动词及其形式里。

items.en: The verb kept an old strong pattern, so the past is began and the participle is begun instead of regular -ed forms.
items.cn: 这个动词保留了古老的强变化，因此过去式是 began、过去分词是 begun，而不是规则的 -ed 形式。

items.en: Middle English kept the verb and added the noun beginning, and the meaning stayed close to starting.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了这个动词，并加出名词 beginning，词义一直贴近「开始」。

items.en: Today begin covers actions, events and origins, while start is the more common verb in everyday speech.
items.cn: 今天 begin 可指动作、事件和起源，而日常口语中 start 更为常用。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the irregular forms and the derived nouns; the near-meaning group collects other verbs for starting.
note.cn: 形近组收不规则形式与派生名词；近义组收其他表示「开始」的动词。

normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的复合成分、不规则形式以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Be- sets about and ginnan means begin, so begin is to set about the first step.
normal.cn: be- 表示「着手」，ginnan 表示「开始」，所以 begin 就是着手迈出第一步。

normal.cn: 拼写是 b-e-g-i-n，中间的 g 只写一个，不要写成两个。

abstract.cn: 想象一条起跑线，一只脚刚刚踏出去，那就是 begin。

abstract.cn: 把「迈出第一步」叠到「故事以一封信开头」上：每个开始都是具体的一步。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the starting line bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让起跑线把意思带回来。

root: begin 来自古英语 beginnan，由 be-「着手」与 ginnan「开始」合成，本义就是迈出第一步。它保留了强变化，过去式 began、过去分词 begun。今天它既指人开始做某事，也指事件自己开始，还可表示「以……为起点」和「起初是」。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of begin keeps the first-step picture: a person starts an action, an event starts itself, a thing is the starting point, or the earliest stage is named.
sensesIntro.cn: begin 的每个义项都保留「第一步」的画面：人去开始一个动作、事件自己开始、某物成为起点，或点明最早的阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one foot leaving the starting line
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚离开起跑线

branches.en: THE ACTOR: a person takes the first step, and an object follows.
branches.cn: 行动线：人迈出第一步，后面带上宾语。

branches.en: THE EVENT: the subject is the thing that starts, with no actor at all.
branches.cn: 事件线：主语就是开始发生的那件事，完全没有执行者。

branches.en: THE POINT: begin with names the ground the first step pushes off from.
branches.cn: 起点线：begin with 点明第一步蹬开的那块地面。

branches.en: THE YOUNG FORM: the earliest stage tells what something first was.
branches.cn: 初形线：最早的阶段说明某物最初是什么样子。

branches.en: THE TWO DIRECTIONS: the same verb moves from a person acting to an event simply happening.
branches.cn: 双向线：同一个动词从「人去做」转到「事件自行发生」。

definition_zh: 举止；表现；守规矩；（机器、物质）表现
definition_en: to act in a particular way, or to act in a polite and controlled way
core_image: 孩子在客人面前坐直身子，把双手放在膝盖上
scene: 家里来了客人，妈妈低声提醒孩子坐好。The children behaved well at the dinner table.
sceneCN: 这里 behave 是「守规矩、表现好」（第 2 个义项：举止得体、听话）；句意为孩子们在餐桌旁表现得很有礼貌。

derivatives.zh: 由 behave 加 -iour 构成，义为「行为；举止」，美式拼作 behavior
由 behaviour 加 -al 构成，义为「行为的」
由 mis-「不当」加 behave 构成，义为「行为不端」
由 well 与 behaved 组合而成，义为「表现好的、听话的」

senses.title: To act in a certain way
senses.definition: to act or conduct oneself in a particular way, whether good or bad
senses.definitionCN: 以某种特定方式行动或表现自己，不论好坏
senses.example: He behaved strangely at the party.
senses.exampleCN: 他在聚会上举止古怪。
senses.why: Old English behabban joined be-, meaning around or for, with habban, to have, so the verb meant to hold or carry oneself, and that is the general sense of acting.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 behabban 由表「在周围、为了」的 be- 与表「持有」的 habban 组成，本义是「把自己拿住」，也就是一般意义上的「举止行事」。

senses.title: To act politely and properly
senses.definition: to act in a polite, controlled way that others approve of
senses.definitionCN: 以有礼貌、有节制、别人认可的方式行事
senses.example: The children behaved well at dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在晚饭时表现很好。
senses.why: Holding oneself in hand is also the picture of good manners, so the general sense narrowed into the everyday sense of behaving properly.
senses.whyCN: 「把自己管住」也正是有教养的样子，于是宽泛的「举止」义收窄成了日常说的「守规矩、表现好」。

senses.title: For a machine or material to perform
senses.definition: for a machine, system, or substance to act or work in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 指机器、系统或物质以某种方式运作或起作用
senses.example: The new engine behaves well in cold weather.
senses.exampleCN: 新发动机在寒冷天气里表现良好。
senses.why: The way a person controls himself is projected onto machines: how a thing conducts itself under conditions is simply how it works.
senses.whyCN: 人控制自己的方式被挪到机器上：某物在特定条件下「自处」的方式，就是它的运作状况。

senses.title: To control oneself
senses.definition: used reflexively in behave oneself, meaning to act properly and stay under control
senses.definitionCN: 用于 behave oneself 这一反身结构，义为举止得体、保持自我约束
senses.example: Behave yourself in front of the guests.
senses.exampleCN: 在客人面前要守规矩。
senses.why: The reflexive form turns the old image of holding oneself back toward the speaker, making self-control the explicit point.
senses.whyCN: 反身形式把「把自己拿住」这个老画面转回说话人自身，让「自我约束」成为明确的意思。

intro.en: Behave began as a compound of be- and have, literally to hold oneself.
intro.cn: behave 最初是 be- 与 have 的复合词，字面意思是「把自己拿住」。

items.en: Old English behabban joined be-, meaning around or for, with habban, meaning to have or hold.
items.cn: 古英语 behabban 由 be-「在周围、为了」与 habban「持有」组成。

items.en: The compound literally meant to hold oneself, that is, to keep oneself under control.
items.cn: 这个复合词字面意为「把握住自己」，也就是「把自己控制在手里」。

items.en: The verb passed into Middle English with the sense of conducting oneself in some way.
items.cn: 这个动词进入中古英语，意思是「以某种方式自处、行事」。

items.en: From conduct in general came the narrower sense of good conduct, and from people came the use for machines and materials.
items.cn: 从一般的「行为」分出较窄的「好行为」，又从人身上扩展到机器与材料。

items.en: Modern English uses behave for conduct in general, for good manners, and for the way things work.
items.cn: 现代英语里 behave 可指一般举止、良好教养，也可指事物的运作表现。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family forms and the mis- compound; the near-meaning group collects verbs that are close to acting or conducting oneself.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词族的各种形式与 mis- 复合词；近义组收与「行事、举止」相近的动词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to possess, which is the second half of behave.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「拥有」，是 behave 的后半部分来源。

entries.definition: The noun for conduct; it spells behavior in American English.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「行为、举止」，美式拼作 behavior。

entries.definition: The regular past tense and past participle.
entries.definitionCN: 规则过去式与过去分词。

entries.definition: To behave badly, formed with the prefix mis-.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「行为不端」，由前缀 mis- 构成。

entries.definition: To do something or to conduct oneself in a way; the closest general synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「行动、表现」，是最接近的一般同义词。

entries.definition: To organize an activity, or to behave in a particular way, in formal use.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，正式用法中义为「进行、表现」，也指组织某项活动。

entries.definition: To carry out an action or to work in a particular way; it matches the machine sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「执行、表现」，对应机器义项。

entries.definition: To act in response to something, a narrower kind of behaving.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「作出反应」，是较窄的一种「表现」。

normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的复合成分、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Be- means around or for, and have means hold: to hold oneself is to behave.
normal.cn: be- 表示「在周围、为了」，have 表示「持有」：把自己拿住就是 behave。

normal.en: Behaviour is the noun, misbehave is the bad verb, and well-behaved is the adjective.
normal.cn: behaviour 是名词，misbehave 是表示「行为不端」的动词，well-behaved 是形容词。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with well, badly, like and oneself.
normal.cn: 它常与 well、badly、like、oneself 搭配。

normal.en: The endings are simple: -s, -ing and -ed, with no doubling of the final e.
normal.cn: 词尾变化很简单：加 -s、-ing、-ed，末尾的 e 不与词干重复。

normal.en: Spell be plus have: two common words joined, and the e in the middle is kept.
normal.cn: 拼写是 be 加 have：两个常见词拼在一起，中间的 e 保留。

abstract.en: See a child sitting straight with both hands on the knees: holding oneself made visible.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子坐直、双手放在膝盖上：把「拿住自己」变成看得见的姿势。

abstract.en: Move the same picture to an engine and it becomes the machine sense of performing.
abstract.cn: 把同一幅画挪到发动机上，就成了机器「表现如何」的义项。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the straight-backed posture bring conduct back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让坐直的姿势把「举止」带回来。

examples.cn: 他在聚会上举止古怪。

examples.en: The children behaved well at dinner.
examples.cn: 孩子们在晚饭时表现很好。

examples.en: The new engine behaves well in cold weather.
examples.cn: 新发动机在寒冷天气里表现良好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必嘿」——在客人面前必嘿地笑，举止得体：举止

root: behave 来自古英语 behabban，由 be-「在周围、为了」加 habban「持有」合成，本义是「把自己拿住」。由「控制自身」引申出一般举止，再分出「守规矩」一义；后来这个「自处的方式」又被用到机器和物质上，表示「表现、性能如何」。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of behave rest on one picture: holding oneself, whether in public, in good manners, inside a machine, or before oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: behave 的四个义项都立在同一个画面上：「把自己拿住」，无论是在众人面前、在礼数上、在机器内部，还是面对自己。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child sitting straight with both hands on the knees
core.cn: 核心意象：一个坐得笔直、双手放在膝盖上的孩子

branches.en: THE GENERAL WAY: holding oneself becomes the neutral sense of acting in some way.
branches.cn: 一般举止线：把自己拿住，变成中性的「以某种方式行事」。

branches.en: THE MANNERS: the same control narrows into acting politely and properly.
branches.cn: 礼仪线：同一种控制收窄成有礼貌、守规矩地行事。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the human picture moves onto engines and materials as how they perform.
branches.cn: 物体线：人的画面挪到发动机与材料上，成为它们的「表现」。

branches.en: THE REFLEXIVE: behave oneself turns the control back toward the speaker.
branches.cn: 反身线：behave oneself 把这份控制转回说话人自身。

branches.en: THE TWO LEVELS: the same verb covers plain conduct and the narrower idea of good conduct.
branches.cn: 两层线：同一个动词既指普通的举止，也指较窄的「好行为」。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 habere「持有」与 behave 的后半部分同出更早的印欧词根，但并非直接借入。

definition_zh: 行为；举止；待人表现；（事物或动物的）活动方式
definition_en: the way that a person, an animal, or a thing acts in a particular situation
core_image: 一面镜子，照出一个人平时怎么说话、怎么坐下
scene: 课间休息时，教室后排的实习老师在记录孩子们的一举一动。The teacher watched the children's behaviour in the playground.
sceneCN: 这里 behaviour 是「行为举止」（第 1 个义项：人在具体场合的举动）；句意为老师观察孩子们在操场上的行为。

derivatives.zh: 本词所由来的动词，义为「举止；表现」
由 behaviour 加 -al 构成，义为「行为的；行为方面的」
由 behaviour 加 -ism 构成，义为「行为主义」
由 behaviour 加 -ist 构成，义为「行为主义者」

senses.title: The way a person acts
senses.definition: the way a person acts in a particular situation, as others see it
senses.definitionCN: 某人在特定场合中行动的方式，尤其是别人看到的样子
senses.example: His behaviour at the meeting surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他在会上的举止让所有人吃惊。
senses.why: The noun was built from behave plus -iour, so it turns the act of holding oneself into something others can watch and describe.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词由 behave 加 -iour 构成，把「把自己拿住」的动作变成别人可以观察和描述的东西。

senses.title: The way one treats others
senses.definition: the way someone acts towards other people, especially in terms of kindness or rudeness
senses.definitionCN: 某人对别人的态度与做法，尤指是否友善或粗鲁
senses.example: Her behaviour towards the new student was kind.
senses.exampleCN: 她对新来的同学很友善。
senses.why: Conduct always points somewhere, and with towards the noun is fixed on the person who receives it, so the sense becomes how one treats others.
senses.whyCN: 举止总是指向某处，加上 towards 后这个名词便固定在接受者身上，义项就成了「怎样对待别人」。

senses.title: Animal behaviour as a pattern
senses.definition: the repeated actions of an animal or group studied as a pattern
senses.definitionCN: 动物或群体反复出现的动作，被当作规律来研究
senses.example: Scientists study the behaviour of birds in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家研究鸟类在冬天的行为。
senses.why: When the same actions repeat under the same conditions, observers stop watching one animal and start describing a pattern, which is the scientific sense.
senses.whyCN: 当同样的动作在同样条件下反复出现，观察者就不再只看一只动物，而是描述一种规律，这就是科学用语里的义项。

senses.title: The way a material or system acts
senses.definition: the way a material, machine, or system reacts under particular conditions
senses.definitionCN: 物质、机器或系统在特定条件下反应的方式
senses.example: The behaviour of the metal changes when it is heated.
senses.exampleCN: 金属受热时，它的表现会发生变化。
senses.why: Once behaviour became a pattern to observe, the same word could describe how a metal or a network responds, so the sense spread from living things to matter.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「行为」成为可观察的规律，同一个词就能描述金属或网络如何反应，于是义项从生物扩展到了物质。

intro.en: Behaviour is an English noun built on the verb behave, with an ending that came through French from Latin.
intro.cn: behaviour 是建立在动词 behave 之上的英语名词，词尾经法语来自拉丁语。

items.en: Middle English formed the noun from behave plus the ending -iour, which named a way of acting.
items.cn: 中古英语用 behave 加词尾 -iour 造出这个名词，表示「行事的方式」。

items.en: That ending goes back to Latin -atura, a suffix that turns an action into its result.
items.cn: 这个词尾可追溯到拉丁语 -atura，它把动作转成动作的结果。

items.en: Early forms such as havior existed without the be-, and the fuller form later became standard.
items.cn: 早期确有 havior 这类不带 be- 的形式，后来带 be- 的完整形式成为标准。

items.en: American English shortened the ending to -ior, giving behavior, while British English kept behaviour.
items.cn: 美式英语把词尾简化为 -ior，写作 behavior；英式英语保留 behaviour。

items.en: Today the noun covers human conduct, animal behaviour, and the way materials act.
items.cn: 今天这个名词覆盖人的举止、动物的行为，以及物质的表现方式。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family forms and the American spelling; the near-meaning group collects nouns for conduct and manner.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词族的形式与美式拼写；近义组收表示「行为、态度」的名词。

entries.definition: A formal noun for the way a person behaves.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，正式用语，义为「行为、举止」。

entries.definition: The polite way of acting in social situations.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「礼貌、规矩」，指社交场合中的得体做法。

entries.definition: A settled way of thinking or feeling that shows in behaviour.

entries.definition: A single thing that someone does.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「行动」，指某人所做的单个举动。

normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的构词方式、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Behave plus -iour gives behaviour: the act turned into a thing you can watch.

normal.en: British English keeps behaviour, and American English writes behavior.

normal.en: It commonly pairs with good, towards, pattern and social.

abstract.en: Imagine a mirror that shows how a person speaks and sits: that is behaviour.
abstract.cn: 想象一面镜子，照出一个人怎么说话、怎么坐下，那就是 behaviour。

abstract.en: Move the mirror from a person to a bird and then to a metal bar: the same picture becomes pattern and reaction.
abstract.cn: 把镜子从人移到鸟，再移到金属条：同一幅画就变成「规律」和「反应」。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the mirror bring the meaning of conduct back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让镜子把「举止」的意思带回来。

examples.en: His behaviour at the meeting surprised everyone.
examples.cn: 他在会上的举止让所有人吃惊。

examples.en: Her behaviour towards the new student was kind.
examples.cn: 她对新来的同学很友善。

examples.en: Scientists study the behaviour of birds in winter.
examples.cn: 科学家研究鸟类在冬天的行为。

root: behaviour 由动词 behave 加词尾 -iour 构成，而 -iour 经法语来自拉丁语 -atura，这个后缀把动作变成动作的结果。因此 behave 的「把自己拿住」变成了可被观察的「举止」。美式英语把词尾简化为 -ior，写作 behavior；今天这个词可用于人、动物和物质。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of behaviour come from one picture: a mirror that shows how something acts when others are watching.
sensesIntro.cn: behaviour 的四个义项都出自同一幅画面：一面镜子，照出某物在别人注视下如何行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mirror that shows how a person speaks and sits
core.cn: 核心意象：一面照出一个人怎么说话、怎么坐下的镜子

branches.en: THE PERSON: the first sense is simply how one person acts in one situation.
branches.cn: 个人线：第一个义项就是一个人在某个场合怎么行动。

branches.en: THE OTHER: conduct pointed at someone becomes the sense of treating people well or badly.
branches.cn: 他人线：举止指向某个人，就变成「待人好或不好的表现」。

branches.en: THE PATTERN: repeated animal actions become a describable rule.
branches.cn: 规律线：动物反复出现的动作变成可描述的规律。

branches.en: THE MATTER: the same observation moves onto metals and systems as reaction.
branches.cn: 物质线：同一种观察挪到金属和系统上，成为「反应」。

branches.en: THE SCALE: one word covers a single act and a whole studied pattern.
branches.cn: 尺度线：同一个词既指单个举动，也指被整体研究的规律。

definition_zh: 在……后面；落后于；迟于；支持；在后面
definition_en: at or to the back of something, or less advanced or later than someone or something
core_image: 一个人站在另一个人背后，被前面的身影挡住
scene: 放学路上，弟弟走在哥哥身后，被前面的身影挡着。The little boy walked behind his brother.
sceneCN: 这里 behind 是「在……后面」（第 1 个义项：位置在某人或某物后方）；句意为小男孩走在哥哥后面。

pos.zh: 介词：在……后面；落后于；迟于；支持

derivatives.zh: 由 behind 与 hand 组合而成，义为「落后的；拖欠的」
由短语 behind the scenes 转成的形容词，义为「幕后的」

senses.title: At the back of something
senses.definition: at or to the back of a person, thing, or place
senses.definitionCN: 在某人、某物或某地的后方，或向后方
senses.example: The bicycle is behind the house.
senses.exampleCN: 自行车在房子后面。
senses.why: Old English behindan joined be-, meaning at, with hindan, meaning from behind, so the word literally says at the back and this place sense is the oldest.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 behindan 由 be-「在」与 hindan「从后面」组成，字面就是「在后面」，所以这个位置义最古老。

senses.title: Less advanced than others
senses.definition: having made less progress, or having a lower score, than someone else
senses.definitionCN: 进度比人少，或分数比人低
senses.example: Our team is two points behind.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队落后两分。
senses.why: In a race or a ranking, the one at the back is also the one who has covered less ground, so the place sense turns into the sense of lagging.
senses.whyCN: 在赛跑或排名里，处在后面的人也正是走得较少的人，于是位置义转成「落后」。

senses.title: Later than expected
senses.definition: later than a planned or expected time
senses.definitionCN: 比计划或预期的时间更晚
senses.example: The train is ten minutes behind schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 火车比时刻表晚了十分钟。
senses.why: On a line of time, a point after the plan is the same picture as a place at the back, so behind also marks lateness.
senses.whyCN: 在时间线上，落在计划点之后，与空间中落在后面是同一幅画面，所以 behind 也标记「迟到」。

senses.title: In support of someone
senses.definition: giving support to a person, plan, or idea
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人、某计划或某想法支持
senses.example: The whole town is behind the new library plan.
senses.exampleCN: 全镇都支持新建图书馆的计划。
senses.why: Standing at someone's back is the physical picture of backing them up, so the place sense grows into the sense of support.
senses.whyCN: 站在某人背后，正是「给他撑腰」的身体画面，于是位置义长成了「支持」义。

senses.title: At the back, standing alone
senses.definition: used as an adverb for staying or moving at the back, without an object
senses.definitionCN: 作副词，不带宾语，表示留在后面或向后面
senses.example: He stayed behind after class.
senses.exampleCN: 下课后他留了下来。
senses.why: With the object dropped, the word still points at the back, and it can now describe staying there rather than being behind a named thing.
senses.whyCN: 去掉宾语后，这个词仍指向后方，只是变成描述「留在那里」，而不是「在某物后面」。

intro.en: Behind is a fused Germanic compound whose two parts both point to the back.
intro.cn: behind 是粘合的日耳曼语复合词，两部分都指向后方。

items.en: Old English behindan joined be-, meaning at, with hindan, meaning from behind.
items.cn: 古英语 behindan 由 be-「在」与 hindan「从后面」组成。

items.en: Hindan belongs to the same family as hinder, and both point to the back or to holding back.
items.cn: hindan 与 hinder 同属一个词族，二者都指向后方或「拦住」。

items.en: The parts fused into one word, which served for place, for rank, and for time.
items.cn: 两部分合并成一个词，同时用于位置、名次和时间。

items.en: Because being at the back means being later or less advanced, behind gained the senses of lagging and of backing someone up.
items.cn: 因为在后面意味着更晚或更落后，behind 又长出「落后」和「支持」两个义项。

items.en: Today behind covers position, lateness, lower rank, and support, and it also works as an adverb.
items.cn: 今天 behind 可指位置、迟到、名次落后与支持，也可作副词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words with the same be- opening or the same ending; the near-meaning group collects words about being after or at the back.
note.cn: 形近组收同样以 be- 开头或词尾相近的词；近义组收表示「在后、之后」的词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning late or in arrears.

entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……旁边」，同样由 be- 前缀构成。

entries.definition: A preposition meaning under, another be- word of place.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……下面」，是另一个带 be- 的位置词。

entries.definition: Later than something in time; it matches the lateness sense.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……之后」，对应「迟于」义。

entries.definition: At a time after the present or after another time.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「后来、更晚」，指现在或另一时间之后。

entries.definition: Towards the back, matching the place sense.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或形容词，义为「向后」，对应位置义。

entries.definition: In front or further forward; the direct opposite of the first sense.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在前面、领先」，是第一个义项的直接反义。

normal.en: Hind and hinder belong to the same old family: one is the back, the other holds back.
normal.cn: hind 与 hinder 同属一个古老词族：一个指后部，一个指拦住。

normal.en: Behind pairs with fall, leave, schedule and scenes.

abstract.en: See one figure standing in the shadow of another: that is behind.
abstract.cn: 想象一个身影站在另一个身影的阴影里，那就是 behind。

abstract.en: Slide the same picture along a track and along a timetable: back, late and lower are one shape.
abstract.cn: 把同一幅画沿着跑道和时刻表滑动：靠后、变晚、名次低其实是同一个形状。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the shadowed figure bring the meaning back.

sensesIntro.en: All five senses of behind stay on one line: the back is also the later place, the lower place, and the place of support.
sensesIntro.cn: behind 的五个义项都留在同一条线上：后面既是较晚的位置，也是较低的位置，还是撑腰的位置。

branches.cn: 后方线：最古老的义项就是某物后面的空间。

branches.en: THE RANK: the one at the back of a race has covered less ground.
branches.cn: 名次线：在队伍后面的人跑过的距离更少。

branches.en: THE CLOCK: a point after the plan is the back of the time line.
branches.cn: 时间线：计划点之后的位置，就是时间线上的后方。

branches.en: THE SUPPORT: standing at someone's back means backing them up.
branches.cn: 支持线：站在某人背后，就是给他撑腰。

branches.en: THE BARE FORM: with no object the word simply means staying at the back.
branches.cn: 独用线：不带宾语时，这个词就只表示留在后面。

definition_zh: 相信；认为；信仰；信任
definition_en: to accept that something is true, or to have confidence in someone
core_image: 一个人把手里的一封信交给另一个人，对方点头收下
scene: 雨天的车站里，陌生人说下一班车还会来，女孩选择相信他。The girl believed the stranger and waited for the next bus.
sceneCN: 这里 believe 是「相信（某人的话）」（第 1 个义项：认为某说法是真的）；句意为女孩相信了陌生人，等着下一班车。

pos.zh: 动词：相信；认为；信仰；信任

derivatives.zh: 由 believe 的词干加 -f 构成，义为「信念；相信」
由 believe 加 -er 构成，义为「信徒；相信的人」
由 believe 加 -able 构成，义为「可信的」
由 un- 加 believable 构成，义为「难以置信的」

senses.title: To accept something as true
senses.definition: to accept that a statement, report, or idea is true
senses.definitionCN: 接受某个说法、报道或想法是真的
senses.example: I believe his story.
senses.exampleCN: 我相信他的说法。
senses.why: Old English belyfan joined be-, an intensifying prefix, with lyfan, to hold dear or trust, so to believe is to hold a claim as something dear and true.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 belyfan 由起强调作用的 be- 与 lyfan「珍视、信任」组成，所以「相信」就是把某个说法当作珍贵而真实的东西握住。

senses.title: To think or suppose
senses.definition: to think that something is probably the case, often with a softer force than know
senses.definitionCN: 认为某事大概是如此，语气通常比 know 更软
senses.example: I believe she is still at school.
senses.exampleCN: 我想她还在学校。
senses.why: If a claim is held as true without proof, the same verb naturally means to think or suppose, because the speaker is stating an opinion rather than a fact.
senses.whyCN: 如果某个说法在没有证据时也被当作真的握住，这个动词自然就表示「认为、猜想」，因为说话人讲的是看法而不是事实。

senses.title: To hold a religious faith
senses.definition: to have faith in a religion, a god, or a set of teachings
senses.definitionCN: 对某种宗教、神或一套教义怀有信仰
senses.example: Her family believes in God.
senses.exampleCN: 她的家人信仰上帝。
senses.why: The strongest form of holding something true needs no evidence at all, and that is exactly the picture of religious faith, so believe in became the verb of belief.
senses.whyCN: 把某件事当作真实来握住的最强形式完全不需要证据，这正是宗教信仰的画面，于是 believe in 成了表达「信仰」的动词。

senses.title: To trust a person
senses.definition: to have confidence that a person is honest or reliable
senses.definitionCN: 有把握地认为某人诚实可靠
senses.example: I believe in you.
senses.exampleCN: 我信任你。
senses.why: Holding a person dear and trusting their word is the human version of holding a claim true, so the verb also means to trust someone.
senses.whyCN: 珍视一个人并信他的话，是「把说法握为真」在人与人之间的版本，所以这个动词也表示「信任某人」。

senses.title: Hard to accept
senses.definition: used in the negative or in questions to say that something is very surprising
senses.definitionCN: 用于否定句或疑问句，表示某事非常令人惊讶
senses.example: I can't believe you finished so fast.
senses.exampleCN: 我真不敢相信你这么快就做完了。
senses.why: When the mind refuses to hold a claim as true, the negated verb becomes the natural way to express surprise at something hard to accept.
senses.whyCN: 当头脑拒绝把某个说法握为真实时，否定形式的这个动词就成了表达「难以接受、令人吃惊」的自然说法。

intro.en: Believe is an old English compound whose second part meant to hold dear, and the noun belief grew beside it.
intro.cn: believe 是古老的英语复合词，后半意为「珍视」，名词 belief 在它旁边长出来。

items.en: Old English belyfan joined be-, used here for intensity, with lyfan, meaning to hold dear or to trust.
items.cn: 古英语 belyfan 由表强调的 be- 与 lyfan「珍视、信任」组成。

items.en: Lyfan is related to the old adjective lief, meaning dear or pleasing, so trust and affection shared one root.
items.cn: lyfan 与古老形容词 lief「亲爱的、可意的」同源，可见信任与喜爱共用一个词根。

items.en: The verb passed into Middle English with the sense of accepting something as true.
items.cn: 这个动词进入中古英语，意思变成「接受某事为真」。

items.en: The noun belief was formed beside the verb, and the pair has stayed together ever since.
items.cn: 名词 belief 在动词旁边形成，这一对词从此一直并行。

items.en: Believe in became the fixed way to speak of faith in God or in a teaching.
items.cn: believe in 成为表达对上帝或某种教义的信仰的固定说法。

items.en: Today believe covers accepting facts, thinking something likely, holding a faith, and trusting a person.
items.cn: 今天 believe 可指接受事实、认为某事很可能、持有信仰，以及信任一个人。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the noun and adjective family; the near-meaning group collects verbs of thinking, trusting, and doubting.
note.cn: 形近组收名词与形容词词族；近义组收表示「认为、信任、怀疑」的动词。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「信徒、相信的人」。

entries.definition: Able to be believed; credible.

entries.definition: To have an opinion, matching the suppose sense.

entries.definition: To have confidence in someone's honesty, matching the person sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「信任」，对应「信任某人」义。

entries.definition: To agree that something is true or right, with less feeling than believe.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「接受、认可」，比 believe 少一些情感。

entries.definition: To think something is probably not true; the opposite of the first sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「怀疑」，是第一个义项的反义。

abstract.cn: 想象一个人把信递给另一个人，对方点头收下，那就是 believe。

abstract.en: Lay the letter over a church and then over a friend's hand: fact, faith and trust are one gesture.
abstract.cn: 把信叠到教堂上，再叠到朋友手上：事实、信仰与信任是同一个动作。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the nodding figure bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让点头的身影把意思带回来。

examples.en: I believe she is still at school.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必理吾」——必先讲道理，我才相信你：相信

root: believe 来自古英语 belyfan，由起强调作用的 be- 与 lyfan「珍视、信任」合成，而 lyfan 又与表示「亲爱的」的 lief 同源，所以「相信」原本就是「把某说法当作珍贵而真实的东西握住」。这一动作落在事实上是「相信」，落在猜测上是「认为」，落在宗教上是「信仰」，落在人身上是「信任」。

sensesIntro.en: All five senses of believe come from one gesture: holding something as true and dear, whether a claim, an opinion, a faith, or a person.
sensesIntro.cn: believe 的五个义项都出自同一个动作：把某样东西当作真实又珍贵地握住，无论是说法、看法、信仰，还是一个人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a letter handed over and accepted with a nod
core.cn: 核心意象：一封信被递过去，对方点头收下

branches.en: THE CLAIM: the plainest sense is accepting a statement as true.
branches.cn: 说法线：最朴素的义项就是把一个说法接受为真。

branches.en: THE OPINION: without proof the same hold becomes a softer think or suppose.
branches.cn: 看法线：没有证据时，同一种「握住」变成较软的「认为、猜想」。

branches.en: THE FAITH: the strongest hold needs no evidence and becomes religious belief.
branches.cn: 信仰线：最强的握住不需要证据，于是成为宗教信仰。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the same confidence placed in a human being is trust.
branches.cn: 信任线：把同一种确信放在一个人身上，就是信任。

branches.en: THE REFUSAL: when the mind will not hold the claim, the negative form expresses surprise.
branches.cn: 拒握线：当头脑不肯握住这个说法时，否定形式就用来表达惊讶。
