definition_zh: 铃；钟；铃声；钟形物
definition_en: a hollow metal object that rings when it is struck or shaken, or the sound it makes
core_image: 门边一枚小铜铃，被手指轻轻一碰就响
scene: 下课铃响了，走廊里一下子热闹起来。The bell rang and the students ran out of the classroom.
sceneCN: 这里 bell 是「铃」（第 1 个义项：敲击或摇动会响的金属器物）；句意为铃响了，学生们跑出教室。

derivatives.zh: 由 door 与 bell 组合而成，义为「门铃」
由 bell 与 boy 组合而成，义为「酒店行李员」
由 bell 与 jar 组合而成，义为「钟罩」

senses.title: The ringing metal object
senses.definition: a hollow metal object, often shaped like a cup, that makes a clear sound when struck or shaken
senses.definitionCN: 一种中空金属器物，多呈杯状，被敲击或摇动时发出清脆声音
senses.example: The bell above the door was broken.
senses.exampleCN: 门上方的铃坏了。
senses.why: Old English belle named the ringing object, and the word itself looks like an imitation of the sound, so the object is the original sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 belle 就指这件会响的东西，词形本身像是在模仿那声响，所以「器物」义最原始。

senses.title: The sound itself
senses.definition: the sound made by a bell, especially as a signal
senses.definitionCN: 铃或钟发出的声音，尤指作为信号的那一声
senses.example: We heard the bell from the tower.
senses.exampleCN: 我们听见钟楼传来的钟声。
senses.why: The object and its sound are so closely tied that one word serves both, so bell can name the ringing as well as the metal that rings.
senses.whyCN: 器物与它的声音贴得太紧，一个词就同时承担两者，所以 bell 既能指那声响，也能指发声的金属。

senses.title: Something shaped like a bell
senses.definition: an object or shape that is wide at the bottom and narrow at the top, like a bell
senses.definitionCN: 下宽上窄、形状像钟的器物或轮廓
senses.example: Cover the young plant with a glass bell.
senses.exampleCN: 用玻璃钟罩把幼苗罩住。
senses.why: Because a bell has a wide skirt and a narrow top, anything with that outline borrowed the name, which is how the shape sense appeared.
senses.whyCN: 因为钟下摆宽、顶部窄，任何具有这个轮廓的东西都借用了这个名字，形状义就是这样产生的。

senses.title: To put a bell on
senses.definition: to attach a bell to an animal or an object
senses.definitionCN: 把铃系在动物或物体上
senses.example: The shepherd belled the lead goat.
senses.exampleCN: 牧人给领头羊系上了铃。
senses.why: The verb is simply the noun turned into action: putting the ringing object onto something so that its sound can be heard.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词转成动作：把会响的器物装到某物上，好让它的声音被听见。

intro.en: Bell is an old Germanic word that probably began as an imitation of the sound.
intro.cn: bell 是古老的日耳曼语词，最初很可能是在模仿那声响。

items.en: Old English belle named the ringing object, and the word looks like an imitation of its sound.
items.cn: 古英语 belle 指会响的器物，词形像是在模仿它发出的声音。

items.en: Dutch bel is a close relative, and both words seem to copy a ringing noise.
items.cn: 荷兰语 bel 是近亲，两个词似乎都在模仿叮当的响声。

items.en: The spelling settled as bell, and the meaning widened to any ringing metal object.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 bell，词义扩展到任何会响的金属器物。

items.en: Church bells marked the hours and called people together, which fixed the word in daily life.
items.cn: 教堂的钟用来报时和召集人，这把这个词牢牢固定在日常生活里。

items.en: Because a bell is wide at the bottom and narrow at the top, the word spread to anything of that shape.
items.cn: 因为钟下宽上窄，这个词扩展到了任何这种形状的东西。

items.en: Today bell covers doorbells, handbells, bell towers, and bell-shaped covers.
items.cn: 今天 bell 可指门铃、手铃、钟楼以及钟形罩。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that sound almost the same; the near-meaning group collects other things that ring or warn.
note.cn: 形近组收读音几乎相同的词；近义组收其他会响或用来示警的东西。

entries.definition: A beautiful woman or the most popular girl, pronounced exactly like bell.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「美女、交际花」，读音与 bell 完全相同。

entries.definition: The front part of the body below the chest.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「肚子、腹部」，开头读音相同。

entries.definition: A strip worn around the waist, or a band of material.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「腰带、带状物」，开头读音相同。

entries.definition: To shout very loudly and deeply.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「大声吼叫」，开头读音相同。

entries.definition: A set of bells, or the musical sound they make.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「编钟、一套钟」，也指它们奏出的乐声。

entries.definition: A large metal disc that rings when struck.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「锣」，一种敲击会响的大金属盘。

entries.definition: An electric device that makes a buzzing signal sound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蜂鸣器」，一种发出嗡嗡信号的电器。

entries.definition: A sound or device that warns people of danger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「警报」，用来提醒危险的声音或装置。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded Germanic origin, the real compounds, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的日耳曼语来源、真实复合词和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Old English belle probably copied the ringing sound, so the word sounds like what it names.
normal.cn: 古英语 belle 很可能是在模仿铃声，所以这个词读起来就像它所指的声音。

normal.en: Dutch bel is a cousin with the same ringing sense.
normal.cn: 荷兰语 bel 是同源近亲，也指会响的铃。

normal.en: Doorbell, bellboy and bell jar all keep the bell picture.
normal.cn: doorbell、bellboy、bell jar 都保留了「铃、钟」的画面。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with ring, door, alarm and tower.
normal.cn: 它常与 ring、door、alarm、tower 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-e-l-l with a double l at the end, like two bells side by side.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-e-l-l，末尾两个 l 并排，像两只并排的铃。

abstract.en: See a small brass bell by a door and a finger about to touch it: that is bell.
abstract.cn: 想象门边一枚小铜铃，手指正要碰上去，那就是 bell。

abstract.en: Turn the same shape upside down onto a plant: the object becomes a cover, and the shape sense follows.
abstract.cn: 把同一个形状倒扣到植物上：器物变成罩子，形状义随之而来。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the sound and the metal come back together.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让声音和金属一起回到脑海里。

examples.en: The bell rang and the students ran out of the classroom.
examples.cn: 铃响了，学生们跑出教室。

examples.en: The bell above the door was broken.
examples.cn: 门上方的铃坏了。

examples.en: We heard the bell from the tower.
examples.cn: 我们听见钟楼传来的钟声。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「贝尔」——贝尔发明的电话一响，就像铃在叫：铃

root: bell 来自古英语 belle，很可能是在模仿铃响的声音，荷兰语 bel 与它同源。这个词最初指会响的金属器物，随后也指它发出的声音；因为它下宽上窄，又引申出「钟形物」；名词转动词后表示「给……系铃」。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of bell come from one small metal object: the thing that rings, the ring it makes, the shape it has, and the act of putting it on.
sensesIntro.cn: bell 的四个义项都出自同一件小金属器物：会响的它、它发出的响、它的形状，以及把铃装上去的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small brass bell by a door, touched by a finger
core.cn: 核心意象：门边一枚小铜铃，被手指轻轻一碰

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the first sense is the hollow metal thing itself.
branches.cn: 器物线：第一个义项就是那件中空金属器物本身。

branches.en: THE SOUND: the same word also names the ringing it produces.
branches.cn: 声音线：同一个词也指它发出的那阵响。

branches.en: THE SHAPE: the wide skirt and narrow top turn into the bell-shaped cover.
branches.cn: 形状线：下摆宽、顶部窄，变成钟形的罩子。

branches.en: THE ACTION: the noun becomes a verb for putting a bell on something.
branches.cn: 动作线：名词转成动词，表示给某物系铃。

branches.en: THE TWO EXTENSIONS: sound and shape are the directions this small object grew in.
branches.cn: 两支线：声音与形状是这件小器物向外生长的两个方向。

intro.en: Bell is a base noun; the items below are its plural, its real compounds, and the words it pairs with.
intro.cn: bell 是基础名词，下面列出的是它的复数、真实复合词以及常与它搭配的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin campana and tintinnabulum are recorded words for bells; English took its word from Germanic, so these are parallels.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 campana 与 tintinnabulum 是有记录的「钟、铃」用词；英语这个词来自日耳曼语，因此二者只是平行词。

items.example: A bell hung above the gate.

items.exampleCN: 它把 bell 变成 bells。
它与 bell 构成 doorbell。
它与 bell 构成 bellboy。

items.example: It forms bell jar with bell.
items.exampleCN: 它与 bell 构成 bell jar。

items.example: The bell tower stands by the church.

items.meaning: a set of bells or their sound

definition_zh: 属于；应放在（某处）；是……的成员；适合
definition_en: to be owned by someone, to be a member of a group, or to be in the right place
core_image: 每件物品上都贴着写有主人名字的标签
scene: 教室的失物招领架上，放着一堆没人认领的文具。The blue scarf belongs to my sister.
sceneCN: 这里 belong 是「属于」（第 1 个义项：所有权归某人）；句意为这条蓝围巾属于我姐姐。

pos.zh: 动词：属于；应放在；是成员；适合

collocations.zh: 属于这里；本来就该在这儿

derivatives.zh: 由 belong 加 -ing 构成，义为「归属感；所有物」
belonging 的复数，义为「随身财物；所有物」

senses.title: To be owned by someone
senses.definition: for an object to be the property of a particular person
senses.definitionCN: 指某件物品是某个人的财产
senses.example: The blue scarf belongs to my sister.
senses.exampleCN: 这条蓝围巾属于我姐姐。
senses.why: Old English gelang meant pertaining or dependent, and belong joined it with be-, so the word first says that a thing hangs on or attaches to an owner.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 gelang 意为「属于、依附于」，belong 让它与 be- 结合，所以这个词最初表示某物挂在或附在某个主人身上。

senses.title: To be in the right place
senses.definition: for an object to have a proper or usual place
senses.definitionCN: 指某件物品有它该在或通常所在的位置
senses.example: This chair belongs in the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 这把椅子应该放在角落里。
senses.why: If a thing attaches to its owner, it can also attach to a place, so the ownership sense gives the sense of the spot where a thing properly stays.
senses.whyCN: 既然东西会附在主人身上，它也会附在某个位置上，于是所有权义给出了「某物本该待在哪里」的义项。

senses.title: To be a member of a group
senses.definition: for a person to be a member of a group, club, family, or team
senses.definitionCN: 指某人是某个团体、俱乐部、家庭或球队的成员
senses.example: She belongs to the school choir.
senses.exampleCN: 她是学校合唱团的成员。
senses.why: Attaching is the same picture for people: a person attaches to a group and becomes one of its members.
senses.whyCN: 「附着」用在人身上是同一幅画：一个人附在一个团体上，就成了它的一员。

senses.title: To suit each other
senses.definition: for two people or things to be right together
senses.definitionCN: 指两个人或两样东西放在一起很合适
senses.example: You and I belong together.
senses.exampleCN: 你和我很相配。
senses.why: When two things each attach to the other, neither is out of place, and that picture is exactly the sense of belonging together.
senses.whyCN: 当两样东西彼此附着，谁都不显得别扭，这幅画正是 belong together「相配」的意思。

intro.en: Belong began as a compound meaning to pertain, and it later spread to ownership and membership.
intro.cn: belong 最初是意为「属于、相关」的复合词，后来扩展到所有权与成员身份。

items.en: Old English gelang meant belonging to or dependent on something.
items.cn: 古英语 gelang 意为「属于某物、依附于某物」。

items.en: Middle English joined be- with a verb from this root, giving belongen, to pertain or to be fitting.
items.cn: 中古英语把 be- 与来自这个词根的动词结合，形成 belongen，意为「相关、合适」。

items.en: The prefix added the idea of being attached around something.
items.cn: 这个前缀增添了「环绕着某物附着」的意思。

items.en: From ownership the verb spread to the right place of an object, membership in a group, and suitability between people.
items.cn: 从所有权出发，这个动词扩展到物体的正确位置、团体中的成员身份，以及人与人之间的合适。

items.en: Today belong almost always appears with to or with a place phrase, and belonging also names a sense of attachment.
items.cn: 今天 belong 几乎总是与 to 或地点短语连用，而 belonging 还表示「归属感」。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family forms and words with the same opening; the near-meaning group collects verbs of ownership and fitting.
note.cn: 形近组收词族形式与同样开头的词；近义组收表示「拥有、适合」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun and participle form, meaning a sense of attachment or a possession.
entries.definitionCN: 名词与分词形式，义为「归属感」或「所有物」。

entries.definition: The plural noun for the things a person owns and carries.
entries.definitionCN: 复数名词，义为「随身财物」。

entries.definition: A preposition meaning under, built with the same be- prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……下面」，同样带 be- 前缀。

entries.definition: A preposition meaning next to, another be- word.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……旁边」，是另一个 be- 词。

entries.definition: To have something as property, matching the ownership sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「拥有」，对应所有权义项。

entries.definition: To have or hold something, more formal than own.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「拥有、持有」，比 own 更正式。

entries.definition: To be connected with or relevant to something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「与……有关、属于」，是较正式的近义词。

entries.definition: To be the right size or shape, matching the suitability sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「合适、合身」，对应「相配」义项。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded root, the real family, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词根、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Old English gelang meant pertaining, and be- adds attachment, so belong means to attach to an owner.
normal.cn: 古英语 gelang 表示「属于、相关」，be- 增添「附着」的意思，所以 belong 就是附在某个主人身上。

normal.en: The same picture covers a group: a person attaches to a team and becomes a member.
normal.cn: 同一幅画也覆盖团体：一个人附在球队上，就成了它的成员。

normal.en: Belonging is the noun for attachment, and belongings are the things you carry.
normal.cn: belonging 是表示「归属」的名词，belongings 则是随身带的财物。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with to, here, together and in.
normal.cn: 它常与 to、here、together、in 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-e-l-o-n-g; the long vowel is written with a single o.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-e-l-o-n-g，长元音只写一个 o。

abstract.en: See a name tag threaded onto every object on a lost-property shelf: that is belong.
abstract.cn: 想象失物招领架上的每件物品都穿着一张写有名字的标签，那就是 belong。

abstract.en: Move the tag from an owner to a shelf and then to a choir: ownership, place and membership share one tag.
abstract.cn: 把标签从主人移到架子，再移到合唱团：所有权、位置和成员身份共用一张标签。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the name tag bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让那张名字标签把意思带回来。

examples.en: The blue scarf belongs to my sister.
examples.cn: 这条蓝围巾属于我姐姐。

examples.en: This chair belongs in the corner.
examples.cn: 这把椅子应该放在角落里。

examples.en: She belongs to the school choir.
examples.cn: 她是学校合唱团的成员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必拢」——该属于你的东西，必拢在自己怀里：属于

root: belong 来自中古英语 belongen，源于古英语 gelang「属于、依附」，并由 be- 增添「附着于」的意思。它最初表示「与某物相关」，随后从所有权扩展到物体的正确位置、团体中的成员身份，以及人与人之间的相配关系。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of belong come from one picture: something attached to something else, whether to an owner, a place, a group, or another thing.
sensesIntro.cn: belong 的四个义项都出自同一幅画面：一物附着在另一物上，无论附着的是主人、位置、团体，还是另一个东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name tag on every object in a lost-property shelf
core.cn: 核心意象：失物招领架上每件物品都贴着名字标签

branches.en: THE OWNER: attaching to a person makes the sense of property.
branches.cn: 主人线：附在一个人身上，就形成「财产」义。

branches.en: THE PLACE: attaching to a spot makes the sense of the right place.
branches.cn: 位置线：附在一个位置上，就形成「应放在此处」义。

branches.en: THE GROUP: attaching to a group makes the sense of membership.
branches.cn: 团体线：附在一个团体上，就形成「成员身份」义。

branches.en: THE MATCH: two things attaching to each other make the sense of fitting together.
branches.cn: 配合线：两样东西彼此附着，就形成「相配」义。

branches.en: THE ONE PICTURE: property and membership are both attachments, one to a person and one to a group.
branches.cn: 同一幅画：所有权与成员身份都是「附着」，一个附在个人，一个附在团体。

intro.en: Belong is a fused compound; the items below are its old parts, its inflections, and the words it commonly joins.
intro.cn: belong 是粘合的复合词，下面列出的是它的古老构件、屈折形式以及常与它组合的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pertinere and proprius are recorded words for pertaining and one's own; they are parallels, not sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pertinere 与 proprius 分别表示「属于」和「自己的」，此处作为平行词列出，而非来源。

items.example: It is the first element of belong.
items.exampleCN: 它是 belong 的第一个成分。

items.example: It is the root behind belong.
items.exampleCN: 它是 belong 背后的词根。

items.meaning: to be owned by, to be a member
items.example: These books belong to the school.

items.exampleCN: 它与 belong 构成 belong to。
它与 belong 构成 belong together。

definition_zh: 在……下面；低于；在下面；下文
definition_en: in or to a lower position than something, or less than a particular amount
core_image: 一张桌子的桌面，和桌面下方的那片地板
scene: 潜水员透过舷窗看见一条小鱼慢慢地游过去。A small fish swam below the boat.
sceneCN: 这里 below 是「在……下面」（第 1 个义项：位置低于某物）；句意为一条小鱼在船下游过。

derivatives.zh: 同源基础词，义为「低的」，是 below 的后半部分来源
由 low 加 -er 构成，义为「较低的」，也可作动词表示「降低」

senses.title: In a lower position
senses.definition: in or to a position that is lower than something else
senses.definitionCN: 在比另一物体更低的位置，或向这样的位置
senses.example: A small fish swam below the boat.
senses.exampleCN: 一条小鱼在船下游过。
senses.why: The word is be-, meaning at, plus low, so it literally says at a low place, and that is the oldest and clearest sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 be-「在」加 low「低」，字面就是「在较低处」，这也是最古老、最清楚的义项。

senses.title: Less than an amount or level
senses.definition: less than a particular number, temperature, standard, or level
senses.definitionCN: 少于某个数字、温度、标准或水平
senses.example: The temperature fell below zero.
senses.exampleCN: 气温降到零度以下。
senses.why: A number on a scale sits above or below another just as an object sits above or below a table, so the place picture turns into the sense of less than.
senses.whyCN: 刻度上的数字像物体在桌面上下的位置一样，也分上下，于是位置画面转成「少于」的意思。

senses.title: At a lower place, standing alone
senses.definition: used as an adverb for something located lower, without an object
senses.definitionCN: 作副词，不带宾语，指位于较低处的东西
senses.example: From the hill we could see the town below.
senses.exampleCN: 从山上我们能看见下面的小镇。
senses.why: With the object dropped, the word still points downward and now simply describes what lies lower than the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 去掉宾语后，这个词仍指下方，只是单纯描述比说话人更低的东西。

senses.title: Further down a page
senses.definition: further down on a page or in a text, used to point readers to later material
senses.definitionCN: 在书页或文本中更靠下的位置，用来指引读者看后面的内容
senses.example: Please read the notes below.
senses.exampleCN: 请读下面的注释。
senses.why: A page is also a vertical space, so the part lower on the page is the part below, and the word came to mean further in the text.
senses.whyCN: 书页本身也是一个竖直的空间，页面上更靠下的一段就是 below，于是这个词也表示「文本更后面」。

intro.en: Below is a compound of be- and low, and it later displaced older English words for the same idea.
intro.cn: below 是 be- 与 low 的复合词，后来取代了英语里几个表示同一意思的旧词。

items.en: Middle English formed the word from be-, meaning at, and low, meaning low.
items.cn: 中古英语用 be-「在」与 low「低」造出这个词。

items.en: The prefix placed the whole word in a spot rather than in a direction.
items.cn: 这个前缀把整个词落在某个位置上，而不只是表示方向。

items.en: Low came from an old Germanic adjective for a flat or low position, and it is still the everyday word.
items.cn: low 来自古老的日耳曼语形容词，表示平坦或低的位置，今天仍是日常用词。

items.en: Old English used other words such as beneothan for below, and the modern form won out only later.
items.cn: 古英语另有 beneothan 等词表示「在下面」，现代形式是后来才胜出的。

items.en: From place the word spread to amounts, standards, and the lower part of a page.
items.cn: 从位置出发，这个词扩展到数量、标准以及书页的下半部分。

items.en: Today below works as a preposition and an adverb, and it often appears in written instructions.
items.cn: 今天 below 可作介词和副词，常出现在书面说明中。

note.en: The look-alike group collects low-family words and similar-sounding forms; the near-meaning group collects other words for a lower position.
note.cn: 形近组收 low 词族的词与读音相近的形式；近义组收其他表示「下方」的词。

entries.definition: The adjective for a small height, the second half of below.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「低的」，是 below 的后半部分来源。

entries.definition: The comparative of low, or a verb meaning to bring down.
entries.definitionCN: low 的比较级，也可作动词表示「降低」。

entries.definition: To shout loudly and deeply.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「大声吼叫」，词尾读音与 below 相近。

entries.definition: To send air out, or a stroke; it sounds close to below.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「吹」，也可作名词指「一击」，读音与 below 接近。

entries.definition: Directly beneath something, often covered by it.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……正下方」，常含被覆盖之意。

entries.definition: Under or lower than something, a more literary word.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……下面」，是较文的用词。

entries.definition: Directly under and usually hidden by something.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「在……底下」，通常含被遮住之意。

entries.definition: At a higher position; the direct opposite of the first sense.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……上面」，是第一个义项的直接反义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded compound parts, the real low family, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的复合成分、真实的 low 词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Be- means at and low means low, so below simply says at a low place.
normal.cn: be- 表示「在」，low 表示「低」，所以 below 就是「在较低处」。

normal.en: Low, lower and below all keep the same height picture.
normal.cn: low、lower、below 都保留同一个「高低」画面。

normal.en: On a page, the lower part is also called below, which is why notes are below.
normal.cn: 在书页上，靠下的部分也叫 below，所以注释总在「下面」。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with zero, average, surface and below.
normal.cn: 它常与 zero、average、surface 搭配，也见于 see below。

normal.en: Spell b-e-l-o-w: be plus low, with the ow at the end.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-e-l-o-w：be 加 low，结尾是 ow。

abstract.en: See a tabletop and the floor under it: the gap itself is below.
abstract.cn: 想象桌面和桌面下方的地板，中间那一块就是 below。

abstract.en: Turn the same picture into a thermometer and then into a page: height becomes number, then position in text.
abstract.cn: 把同一幅画换成温度计，再换成书页：高度先变成数字，再变成文中的位置。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the floor under the table bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让桌面下的地板把意思带回来。

examples.en: A small fish swam below the boat.
examples.cn: 一条小鱼在船下游过。

examples.en: The temperature fell below zero.
examples.cn: 气温降到零度以下。

examples.en: Please read the notes below.
examples.cn: 请读下面的注释。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必漏」——水必漏到桌子下面去：在……下面

root: below 由 be-「在」与 low「低」合成，字面就是「在较低处」。它在中古英语成形，逐渐取代了 beneothan 等旧说法。由「位置低」引申出「数量、水平低于」，也能单独作副词；书页靠下的一段同样叫 below，因此可以表示「见下文」。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of below stay on one vertical line: lower than a thing, lower than a number, lower than the speaker, lower on a page.
sensesIntro.cn: below 的四个义项都留在同一条竖直线上：比物体低、比数字低、比说话人低、在页面上更靠下。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tabletop and the floor beneath it
core.cn: 核心意象：一张桌子的桌面和桌面下方的地板

branches.en: THE PLACE: the plainest sense is a spot lower than an object.
branches.cn: 位置线：最朴素的义项就是比某物更低的地方。

branches.en: THE SCALE: a number lower on a scale becomes less than a level.
branches.cn: 刻度线：刻度上更低的数字变成「少于某个水平」。

branches.en: THE VIEW: with no object the word describes whatever lies lower in sight.
branches.cn: 视野线：不带宾语时，这个词描述视野中更低的东西。

branches.en: THE PAGE: the lower part of a page becomes the later part of a text.
branches.cn: 页面线：书页靠下的部分变成文本更靠后的部分。

branches.en: THE SAME AXIS: space and number share one vertical picture of high and low.
branches.cn: 同一轴线：空间与数字共用一幅「上下」的竖直画面。

intro.en: Below is a fused compound of be- and low; the items below are those parts and the words built on low.
intro.cn: below 是 be- 与 low 的粘合复合词，下面列出的是这些成分以及建立在 low 之上的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin infra and sub are recorded words for below and under; they are parallels, not sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 infra 与 sub 分别表示「在……下面」和「在……之下」，此处作为平行词列出，而非来源。

items.exampleCN: 它是 below 的第一个成分。

items.example: The wall is low enough to jump.
items.exampleCN: 这堵墙矮得可以跳过去。

items.example: The keys are below the table.

items.exampleCN: 它由 low 构成 lower。

items.meaning: less high, or to bring down

items.example: The cat slept beneath the chair.
It appears in submarine and subway.
items.exampleCN: 它见于 submarine 与 subway。

items.example: It appears in infrastructure and infrared.
items.exampleCN: 它见于 infrastructure 与 infrared。

definition_zh: 在……旁边；与……相比；与……无关；情绪失控
definition_en: next to or at the side of someone or something
core_image: 两个人并排坐在同一条长凳上
scene: 公园的长椅上，两个孩子分着一块面包。A girl sat beside her friend on the bench.
sceneCN: 这里 beside 是「在……旁边」（第 1 个义项：位置紧挨着某人）；句意为一个女孩在长椅上坐在朋友旁边。

pos.zh: 介词：在……旁边；与……相比；beside oneself 情绪失控

derivatives.zh: 由 beside 加 -s 构成，义为「此外」，也可作介词表示「除……之外」
同源基础词，义为「侧面；一边」，是 beside 的后半部分来源

senses.title: Next to someone or something
senses.definition: at the side of a person or thing, close to it
senses.definitionCN: 在某个人或某件物品的侧面，离它很近
senses.example: A girl sat beside her friend on the bench.
senses.exampleCN: 一个女孩在长椅上坐在朋友旁边。
senses.why: Old English wrote be sidan, meaning by the side, so the word literally points at the flank of something, and this place sense is the original one.
senses.whyCN: 古英语写作 be sidan，意思是「在侧面」，所以这个词字面就指向某物的侧边，位置义是其本义。

senses.title: Compared with someone
senses.definition: used to compare two people or things placed next to each other
senses.definitionCN: 用于把并排放在一起的两个人或两样东西作比较
senses.example: Beside her sister, she seemed very quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 和姐姐相比，她显得很文静。
senses.why: When two things stand side by side, the eye moves from one to the other and compares them, so the place sense turns into the sense of compared with.
senses.whyCN: 当两样东西并排站着，视线自然从一边移到另一边作比较，于是位置义转成「与……相比」。

senses.title: Beside the point
senses.definition: used in beside the point for something not connected to the matter being discussed
senses.definitionCN: 用于 beside the point，表示与正在讨论的事情没有关系
senses.example: His age is beside the point.
senses.exampleCN: 他的年龄与此无关。
senses.why: Something placed beside the point is off the line of the argument, so the place picture became a fixed way to say irrelevant.
senses.whyCN: 被放在「要点旁边」的东西就偏离了论证的正线，于是这个位置画面固定成表示「无关」的说法。

senses.title: Beside oneself
senses.definition: used in beside oneself to say that someone is so upset that they are not in control
senses.definitionCN: 用于 beside oneself，表示某人激动到无法控制自己
senses.example: She was beside herself with worry.
senses.exampleCN: 她担心得不知所措。
senses.why: Beside oneself literally means standing outside oneself, and that is exactly the picture of feelings so strong that self-control is lost.
senses.whyCN: beside oneself 字面是「站在自己旁边」，正是情绪太强以致失去自控的画面。

intro.en: Beside began as two words meaning by the side, and the -s form besides grew beside it.
intro.cn: beside 最初是两个词，意思是「在侧面」，而带 -s 的 besides 在它旁边长出来。

items.en: Old English wrote be sidan as two words, meaning by the side.
items.cn: 古英语把 be sidan 写成两个词，意思是「在侧面」。

items.en: Sidan is the old form of side, the flank of the body or of a place.
items.cn: sidan 是 side 的古形，指身体或某处的侧面。

items.en: The two words fused into beside, and the final e is what remains of the old ending.
items.cn: 两个词粘合成 beside，词尾的 e 是古老词尾留下的痕迹。

items.en: A form with -s grew beside it and took the sense of in addition or apart from.
items.cn: 带 -s 的形式在它旁边长出，取得「此外、除……之外」的意思。

items.en: From position beside a thing came comparison, and the fixed phrase beside the point.
items.cn: 从「在某物旁边」的位置，引申出比较，以及固定说法 beside the point。

items.en: Today beside is a preposition of position, and beside oneself is a fixed phrase for losing control.
items.cn: 今天 beside 是表示位置的介词，beside oneself 则是表示失控的固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects side-family forms; the near-meaning group collects other prepositions of near position.
note.cn: 形近组收 side 词族的形式；近义组收其他表示「靠近」的介词。

entries.definition: An adverb and preposition meaning in addition or except.
entries.definitionCN: 副词与介词，义为「此外、除……之外」。

entries.definition: The flank or surface of something, the core of beside.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「侧面、一边」，是 beside 的核心成分。

entries.definition: To one side, or a remark not meant for everyone.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「到一边」，也可指不当众的旁白。

entries.definition: Next to and along the side of something.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……旁边、与……并排」。

entries.definition: Directly at the side of something; the closest everyday synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 短语介词，义为「紧挨着」，是最接近的日常同义说法。

entries.definition: Close to something, but not necessarily at its side.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「靠近」，但不一定就在侧面。

entries.definition: Close to or past something, often used for people and places.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……旁边、经过」，常用于人和地点。

entries.definition: Facing something from the other side.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……对面」，与「在旁边」相对。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded two-word origin, the side family, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的两词来源、side 词族以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Be sidan meant by the side, and side is still visible inside beside.
normal.cn: be sidan 的意思是「在侧面」，而 side 至今仍能在 beside 里看见。

normal.en: The -s form besides took the different sense of in addition.
normal.cn: 带 -s 的 besides 取了另一个意思「此外」。

normal.en: Side by side leads naturally to comparison, hence beside her sister.
normal.cn: 并排而立自然带来比较，所以有 beside her sister 的说法。

normal.en: Beside the point and beside oneself are two fixed phrases worth learning whole.
normal.cn: beside the point 与 beside oneself 是两个值得整句记住的固定说法。

normal.en: Spell b-e-s-i-d-e: be plus side, with the final e kept.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-e-s-i-d-e：be 加 side，末尾的 e 保留。

abstract.en: See two children sharing one bench: their shoulders almost touch, and that is beside.
abstract.cn: 想象两个孩子共用一条长凳，肩膀几乎碰到，那就是 beside。

abstract.en: Move one child out of the frame of the argument: beside becomes irrelevant.
abstract.cn: 把一个孩子挪出讨论的框外，beside 就变成「无关」。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the shared bench bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让那条共用的长凳把意思带回来。

examples.en: A girl sat beside her friend on the bench.
examples.cn: 一个女孩在长椅上坐在朋友旁边。

examples.en: Beside her sister, she seemed very quiet.
examples.cn: 和姐姐相比，她显得很文静。

examples.en: His age is beside the point.
examples.cn: 他的年龄与此无关。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必晒的」——坐在太阳旁边，必被晒到：在……旁边

root: beside 来自古英语的两个词 be sidan，意为「在侧面」，其中 sidan 就是今天的 side。两部分粘合后写作 beside，末尾的 e 是旧词尾的残留。带 -s 的形式 besides 另取「此外」之义；而并排的位置又引申出「与……相比」和 beside the point「无关」、beside oneself「失控」两个固定说法。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of beside start at the side of something: next to it, compared with it, off the point, or outside oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: beside 的四个义项都从「某物的侧面」出发：在它旁边、与它相比、偏离要点，或站到自己之外。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people sitting shoulder to shoulder on one bench
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人肩并肩坐在同一条长凳上

branches.en: THE SIDE: the first sense is simply the space right at something's flank.
branches.cn: 侧面线：第一个义项就是紧挨某物侧边的空间。

branches.en: THE COMPARISON: two things side by side invite the eye to compare them.
branches.cn: 比较线：两样东西并排，会引着视线去比较。

branches.en: THE POINT: placed beside the point means off the line of the argument.
branches.cn: 要点线：被放在要点旁边，就是偏离论证的正线。

branches.en: THE SELF: standing beside oneself is the picture of losing self-control.
branches.cn: 自身线：站在自己旁边，正是失去自控的画面。

branches.en: THE DOUBLE USE: the same place word serves plain position and comparison.
branches.cn: 双用线：同一个位置词既指单纯的位置，也指比较。

intro.en: Beside is a fused compound of be- and side; the items below are those parts and the words built on side.
intro.cn: beside 是 be- 与 side 的粘合复合词，下面列出的是这些成分以及建立在 side 之上的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin juxta and prope are recorded words for beside and near; they are parallels, not sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 juxta 与 prope 分别表示「在……旁边」和「靠近」，此处作为平行词列出，而非来源。

items.example: It is the second element of beside.

items.example: The box has a label on every side.

items.example: The boat lay alongside the wall.

definition_zh: 在……之间（空间）；在……之间（时间）；介于两者关系；数量介于
definition_en: in the space or time that separates two things, or in a relationship involving two or more sides
core_image: 两栋房子之间的一条窄巷
scene: 两栋房子之间有一条铺着石板的小巷，孩子们在里面来回跑。A narrow lane runs between the two houses.
sceneCN: 这里 between 是「在……之间（空间）」（第 1 个义项：位于两物之间的位置）；句意为一条窄巷位于两栋房子之间。

collocations.zh: 私下说；只在你我之间说
在两次工作之间；暂时失业

derivatives.zh: 由 in 与 between 组合而成，义为「介于两者之间的东西」，也可作形容词
同源异体词，义为「在……之间」，多见于古旧或文学用法

senses.title: In the space separating two things
senses.definition: in the space that separates two places, objects, or people
senses.definitionCN: 在把两个地方、物体或人分开的空间里
senses.example: A narrow lane runs between the two houses.
senses.exampleCN: 一条窄巷位于两栋房子之间。
senses.why: Old English betweonum joined be-, at, with tweonum, a form meaning by two, so the word literally places something among two things.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 betweonum 由 be-「在」与表示「两者」的 tweonum 组成，所以这个词字面就是把某物放在两样东西中间。

senses.title: In the time separating two points
senses.definition: in the period that separates two times or events
senses.definitionCN: 在把两个时间点或两件事分开的那段时间里
senses.example: The shop is closed between noon and two.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店中午两点之间关门。
senses.why: Two points on a line of time have a stretch between them just as two houses have a lane between them, so the space sense carries over to time.
senses.whyCN: 时间线上的两个点之间有一段距离，就像两栋房子之间有一条巷子，于是空间义直接搬到时间上。

senses.title: In a relation or a difference
senses.definition: used for a relationship, a difference, or a choice involving two sides
senses.definitionCN: 用于涉及两方的关系、差别或选择
senses.example: What is the difference between these two words?
senses.exampleCN: 这两个词之间有什么区别？
senses.why: The gap between two things also holds whatever connects or separates them, so between marks comparison, difference, and choice.
senses.whyCN: 两物之间的空隙里，也装着连接或分开它们的东西，所以 between 用来标记比较、差别与选择。

senses.title: Shared by two sides
senses.definition: used when two sides share or divide something, as in divide between them
senses.definitionCN: 用于两方共同拥有或分担某物，如 divide between them
senses.example: They divided the money between them.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把钱分了。
senses.why: What is placed in the space between two sides can be taken by both, so between also marks sharing and division.
senses.whyCN: 放在两方之间那块空地上的东西，两边都能拿，所以 between 也标记「共有、分担」。

senses.title: In a range of numbers
senses.definition: used for an amount that lies inside a range with two ends
senses.definitionCN: 用于处在有上下两端的范围之内的数量
senses.example: The trip takes between three and four hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟路程要三到四个小时。
senses.why: A range has two ends, and the amount sits in the gap between them, which is the same picture applied to numbers.
senses.whyCN: 一个范围有上下两端，数量正好落在两端之间的空隙里，这就是同一幅画用在数字上。

intro.en: Between is an old compound whose middle still contains the word for two.
intro.cn: between 是古老的复合词，中间至今藏着表示「二」的词。

items.en: Old English betweonum joined be-, meaning at, with tweonum, a form meaning by two.
items.cn: 古英语 betweonum 由 be-「在」与表示「两者」的 tweonum 组成。

items.en: The related word twegen, two, is still visible in the middle of between.
items.cn: 相关词 twegen「二」至今仍能在 between 中间看见。

items.en: The form shortened to between, and the sense stayed on the space or time separating two points.
items.cn: 形式缩短为 between，词义仍留在分开两点的空间或时间上。

items.en: From physical space the word spread to time, to comparison, to sharing, and to ranges of number.
items.cn: 从物理空间出发，这个词扩展到时间、比较、共同分担以及数量范围。

items.en: Today between is one of the commonest prepositions, and in-between also works as a noun and an adjective.
items.cn: 今天 between 是最常用的介词之一，in-between 还可作名词和形容词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words sharing the tween element; the near-meaning group collects words for being among or in the middle.
note.cn: 形近组收共享 tween 成分的词；近义组收表示「在……之中、在中间」的词。

entries.definition: A child between the ages of about ten and twelve.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「十到十二岁之间的孩子」，与 between 共享 tween 成分。

entries.definition: The number that sits inside the old form of between.
entries.definitionCN: 数词，义为「二」，藏在 between 的古老形式里。

entries.definition: An old or literary word for between.
entries.definitionCN: 古老或文学性的 between 说法。

entries.definition: Something that sits in the middle of two other things.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「介于两者之间的（东西）」。

entries.definition: In the middle of a group of more than two things.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……之中」，用于三者或更多。

entries.definition: In the middle of something, often a situation or a crowd.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……之中」，多用于情境或人群。

entries.definition: At the middle point between two places.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在中途」，指两地之间的中点。

entries.definition: The central part or point of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「中间、中部」，指某物的中心部分。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded compound parts, the hidden word for two, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的复合成分、藏在词里的「二」以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Be- means at and the old tweonum means by two, so between is at the place of two.
normal.cn: be- 表示「在」，古老的 tweonum 表示「两者」，所以 between 就是「在两者的位置上」。

normal.en: The word two is still visible in the middle of between, which is why it always needs two sides.
normal.cn: two 至今能在 between 中间看见，所以它总是需要两方。

normal.en: Three or more things take among, while two things take between.
normal.cn: 三者或更多用 among，两者则用 between。

normal.en: It commonly appears in between you and me, between jobs and in between.
normal.cn: 它常出现在 between you and me、between jobs、in between 这些说法里。

normal.en: Spell b-e-t-w-e-e-n with a double e in the middle.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-e-t-w-e-e-n，中间两个 e 相连。

abstract.en: See a stone lane squeezed between two houses: the lane is the meaning.
abstract.cn: 想象两栋房子之间挤着一条石板小巷，那条巷子就是这个词的意思。

abstract.en: Stretch the lane along a clock and then along a ruler: space, time and number all have two ends.
abstract.cn: 把这条巷子沿着时钟拉长，再沿着尺子拉长：空间、时间与数量都有两端。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the narrow lane bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让那条窄巷把意思带回来。

examples.en: A narrow lane runs between the two houses.
examples.cn: 一条窄巷位于两栋房子之间。

examples.en: The shop is closed between noon and two.
examples.cn: 这家店中午两点之间关门。

examples.en: What is the difference between these two words?
examples.cn: 这两个词之间有什么区别？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必传闻」——必在两人之间传话：在……之间

root: between 来自古英语 betweonum，由 be-「在」与表示「两者」的 tweonum 合成，中间还藏着 twegen「二」的痕迹，所以它天生需要两方。由两物之间的空间，它扩展到时间间隔、比较与差别、两方共有，以及有上下两端的数量范围。

sensesIntro.en: All five senses of between come from one picture: a gap with two ends, whether the ends are houses, hours, sides, or numbers.
sensesIntro.cn: between 的五个义项都出自同一幅画面：两端之间的一段空隙，无论两端是房子、时刻、两方还是数字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone lane squeezed between two houses
core.cn: 核心意象：两栋房子之间一条挤出来的石板小巷

branches.en: THE SPACE: the first sense is the gap that separates two places.
branches.cn: 空间线：第一个义项就是分开两个地点的空隙。

branches.en: THE TIME: two points in time have a stretch between them as well.
branches.cn: 时间线：两个时间点之间同样有一段距离。

branches.en: THE RELATION: the gap also holds comparison, difference and choice.
branches.cn: 关系线：那道空隙里也装着比较、差别与选择。

branches.en: THE SHARING: what lies in the gap can be taken by both sides.
branches.cn: 共有线：落在空隙里的东西，两边都能取。

branches.en: THE RANGE: two ends of a scale make a gap for numbers to sit in.
branches.cn: 范围线：刻度的两端造出一道空隙，让数字落在里面。

intro.en: Between is a fused compound; the items below are its old parts and the words built on them.
intro.cn: between 是粘合的复合词，下面列出的是它的古老构件以及建立在这些成分上的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin inter and intra are recorded prefixes for between and within; they are parallels, not sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inter 与 intra 分别表示「在……之间」和「在……之内」，此处作为平行词列出，而非来源。

items.example: It is the first element of between.
items.exampleCN: 它是 between 的第一个成分。

items.example: It is the second element of between.
items.exampleCN: 它是 between 的第二个成分。

items.example: Two chairs stood by the wall.

items.meaning: in the middle of two things
items.example: The shop sits between a bank and a school.
items.exampleCN: 这家店位于银行和学校之间。

items.example: It appears in international and interact.
items.exampleCN: 它见于 international 与 interact。

items.example: It appears in intranet and intravenous.
items.exampleCN: 它见于 intranet 与 intravenous。

definition_zh: 自行车；骑自行车；自行车的
definition_en: a vehicle with two wheels that a person moves by pushing pedals
core_image: 两个轮子一前一后，链条把脚踏的力量送到后轮
scene: 清晨的巷口，男孩跨上自行车，脚一蹬就滑了出去。He rides his bicycle to school every morning.
sceneCN: 这里 bicycle 是「自行车」（第 1 个义项：两轮脚踏车）；句意为他每天早上骑自行车上学。

forms.label: 过去式与过去分词（动词）

derivatives.zh: 由 bicycle 加 -ist 构成，义为「骑自行车的人」
同族词，由 tri-「三」加 cycle 构成，义为「三轮车」
同族词，由 uni-「一」加 cycle 构成，义为「独轮车」

senses.title: The two-wheeled pedal vehicle
senses.definition: a vehicle with two wheels in line, moved by pedals and steered by handlebars
senses.definitionCN: 一种两轮前后排列、靠脚踏驱动、用把手转向的车
senses.example: He rides his bicycle to school every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天早上骑自行车上学。
senses.why: The name joins bi-, two, with cycle, wheel, so it literally says two wheels, which is the plainest description of the machine.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字把表示「二」的 bi- 与表示「轮」的 cycle 合在一起，字面就是「两个轮子」，正是对这种车最直白的描述。

senses.title: To ride a bicycle
senses.definition: to travel or move by bicycle
senses.definitionCN: 骑自行车出行或移动
senses.example: She bicycled across the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 她骑自行车过了桥。
senses.why: The verb is the noun turned into action: using the two-wheeled machine to get somewhere.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词转成动作：用这种两轮车去到某个地方。

senses.title: Used as a modifier
senses.definition: used before another noun to mean intended for or belonging to bicycles
senses.definitionCN: 用在另一个名词前，表示供自行车使用或属于自行车的
senses.example: The bicycle lane is painted green.
senses.exampleCN: 自行车道被刷成了绿色。
senses.why: English lets a noun stand before another noun like an adjective, so bicycle before lane simply marks what the lane is for.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许名词像形容词一样放在另一个名词前，所以 lane 前的 bicycle 只是标记这条道是给谁用的。

intro.en: Bicycle is a nineteenth-century coinage built from a Latin prefix and a Greek word for wheel.
intro.cn: bicycle 是十九世纪造出的词，由拉丁语前缀与希腊语「轮」合成。

items.en: French coined bicyclette in the nineteenth century from bi-, two, and cycle, wheel.
items.cn: 法语在十九世纪用 bi-「二」与 cycle「轮」造出 bicyclette。

items.en: The first part is the Latin prefix bi-, meaning two, related to bis, twice.
items.cn: 第一部分是拉丁语前缀 bi-，意为「二」，与 bis「两次」相关。

items.en: The second part goes back to Greek kyklos, a circle or a wheel.
items.cn: 第二部分可追溯到希腊语 kyklos，意为「圆圈、轮子」。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the age of the pedalled machine and shortened it to bicycle.
items.cn: 英语在脚踏车流行的年代借入这个词，并缩短为 bicycle。

items.en: Everyday speech soon clipped it to bike, which became the common short form.
items.cn: 日常口语很快把它截短为 bike，此后成为常用的简短形式。

items.en: Today bicycle is the formal word, and it also works as a verb and as a modifier.
items.cn: 今天 bicycle 是正式用词，也可作动词和定语。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the short form and the trike family; the near-meaning group collects other small wheeled vehicles.
note.cn: 形近组收简短形式与三轮车一族；近义组收其他小型轮式交通工具。

entries.definition: The clipped everyday word for a bicycle or motorcycle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「自行车、摩托车」，是 bicycle 的日常截短形式。

entries.definition: A wheel word used in bicycle, and also a verb meaning to ride.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「轮、循环」，是 bicycle 的后半成分，也可作动词表示「骑车」。

entries.definition: A three-wheeled pedal vehicle, built with tri-.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「三轮车」，由 tri-「三」构成。

entries.definition: A person who rides a bicycle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「骑自行车的人」。

entries.definition: Any vehicle with two wheels, used as a general name.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「两轮车」，是泛指的说法。

entries.definition: A small motor vehicle with pedals and a low engine.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「轻便摩托车」，带脚踏和小排量发动机。

entries.definition: A small two-wheeled vehicle that the rider stands or sits on.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「踏板车、小轮摩托」，骑者站在或坐在上面。

entries.definition: A heavy two-wheeled vehicle driven by an engine.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「摩托车」，由发动机驱动的重型两轮车。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded parts, the real family, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的构件、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Bi- means two and cycle means wheel, so bicycle is simply two wheels.
normal.cn: bi- 表示「二」，cycle 表示「轮」，所以 bicycle 就是「两个轮子」。

normal.en: Tricycle adds tri-, three, and unicycle adds uni-, one; the family is easy to see.
normal.cn: tricycle 换成 tri-「三」，unicycle 换成 uni-「一」，这个词族一眼就能看清。

normal.en: Everyday speech shortens it to bike, which is the word you hear most.
normal.cn: 日常口语把它缩短成 bike，这是最常听到的说法。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with ride, lane, pump and shop.
normal.cn: 它常与 ride、lane、pump、shop 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-i-c-y-c-l-e: two c's and one y, with the y between them.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-i-c-y-c-l-e：两个 c，中间夹一个 y。

abstract.en: See two wheels in a line with a chain running between them: that is bicycle.
abstract.cn: 想象两个轮子前后排列，中间有一条链条，那就是 bicycle。

abstract.en: Turn the same picture into a verb and the wheels start moving under a rider.
abstract.cn: 把同一幅画变成动词，两个轮子就在骑者脚下转起来。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the turning wheels bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让转动的车轮把意思带回来。

examples.en: He rides his bicycle to school every morning.
examples.cn: 他每天早上骑自行车上学。

examples.en: She bicycled across the bridge.
examples.cn: 她骑自行车过了桥。

examples.en: The bicycle lane is painted green.
examples.cn: 自行车道被刷成了绿色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拜四轮」——拜服这四个轮子？其实只有两个：自行车

root: bicycle 是十九世纪的造词，来自法语 bicyclette，由拉丁语前缀 bi-「二」与希腊语 kyklos「轮」合成，字面就是「两个轮子」。英语借入后缩短为 bicycle，口语又进一步截成 bike。名词可作定语，也可直接转动词表示「骑自行车」。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses of bicycle are one machine seen three ways: the thing itself, the act of riding it, and its use as a modifier.
sensesIntro.cn: bicycle 的三个义项是同一台车的三种看法：车本身、骑它的动作，以及它作定语时的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two wheels in a line joined by a chain
core.cn: 核心意象：两个前后排列、由链条相连的轮子

branches.en: THE MACHINE: two wheels and pedals make the object itself.
branches.cn: 机器线：两个轮子加脚踏，构成这件器物本身。

branches.en: THE MOTION: the same machine turning into an action becomes the verb.
branches.cn: 动作线：同一台车转成动作，就成了动词。

branches.en: THE PURPOSE: placed before lane or shop, the noun marks what something is for.
branches.cn: 用途线：放在 lane 或 shop 前，这个名词标记某物的用途。

branches.en: THE PAIR: the object and its action share one word in English.
branches.cn: 成对线：器物与动作在英语里共用同一个词。

branches.en: THE RIDER: the moving picture always needs a person on the seat.
branches.cn: 骑者线：会动的画面里总要有一个坐在座上的人。

intro.en: Bicycle is a modern compound of a Latin prefix and a wheel word, so its parts are productive in many other words.
intro.cn: bicycle 是由拉丁语前缀与「轮」词构成的现代复合词，其构件在许多其他词里也能产。

latinIntro.en: Latin bis and bi- give the two, and the Latinized Greek cyclus gives the wheel; all three are listed below.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 bis 与 bi- 提供「二」的意思，拉丁化的希腊词 cyclus 提供「轮」的意思，三者均列于下。

items.example: It appears in bicycle and bilingual.
items.exampleCN: 它见于 bicycle 与 bilingual。

items.example: It is the second element of bicycle.
items.exampleCN: 它是 bicycle 的第二个成分。

items.example: A bicycle stood by the wall.

definition_zh: 大的；重要的；年长的；程度大的；志向大的
definition_en: large in size, amount, or importance
core_image: 一头大象站在一群小鸟旁边
scene: 动物园里，孩子们仰头看那头巨大的象。An elephant is a very big animal.
sceneCN: 这里 big 是「体积大的」（第 1 个义项：尺寸或体积大）；句意为大象是一种很大的动物。

pos.zh: 形容词：大的；重要的；年长的；程度大的

derivatives.zh: 由 big 与 hearted 组合而成，义为「宽厚的；慷慨的」
由 big 与 name 组合而成，义为「有名的；大牌的」

senses.title: Large in size
senses.definition: taking up a lot of space, or being of great size
senses.definitionCN: 占据很大空间，或尺寸很大
senses.example: An elephant is a very big animal.
senses.exampleCN: 大象是一种很大的动物。
senses.why: Big appears in Middle English as a plain word for strong and bulky, and although its deeper origin is uncertain, size is the sense it has always carried most plainly.
senses.whyCN: big 在中古英语里就是表示「强壮、粗大」的普通词，虽然更早的来源不确定，但「尺寸大」始终是它最直白的意思。

senses.title: Important or serious
senses.definition: important, serious, or having great influence
senses.definitionCN: 重要的、严重的，或影响很大的
senses.example: Moving house is a big decision.
senses.exampleCN: 搬家是一个重大的决定。
senses.why: Something that takes up a lot of space also takes up a lot of attention, so the size picture became the sense of importance.
senses.whyCN: 占据很大空间的东西也占去很多注意力，于是「大」的画面就变成了「重要」的意思。

senses.title: Older
senses.definition: older, used especially of a brother or sister
senses.definitionCN: 年纪较大的，尤用于哥哥或姐姐
senses.example: My big brother is at university.
senses.exampleCN: 我哥哥在上大学。
senses.why: In a family the older child is usually the larger one, so the word for size became the everyday word for the older sibling.
senses.whyCN: 在家里，年长的孩子通常个子更大，于是表示尺寸的词就成了称呼年长手足的日常说法。

senses.title: Great in degree
senses.definition: great in amount, degree, or strength
senses.definitionCN: 在数量、程度或强度上很大
senses.example: There is a big difference between the two plans.
senses.exampleCN: 两个方案之间有很大差别。
senses.why: Amounts and differences can be pictured as piles, and a large pile is a big one, so the size word covers degree as well.
senses.whyCN: 数量和差别可以画成一堆堆的东西，堆得高的就是大的，所以这个尺寸词也覆盖「程度」。

senses.title: Ambitious in scope
senses.definition: large in ambition, scope, or imagination
senses.definitionCN: 在抱负、规模或想象上很大
senses.example: He has big ideas for the future.
senses.exampleCN: 他对未来有宏大的想法。
senses.why: Once size can describe amount, it can also describe plans and dreams, so big ideas are plans drawn on a large scale.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「大」能描述数量，它也能描述计划与梦想，所以 big ideas 就是按大尺度画出的计划。

intro.en: Big is a Middle English word of uncertain deeper origin, and it slowly replaced older words for size.
intro.cn: big 是中古英语的词，更早的来源不确定，它逐渐取代了英语里表示「大」的旧词。

items.en: Big appears in Middle English, and its deeper origin is uncertain; it may be related to a northern word for strong.
items.cn: big 见于中古英语，更早的来源不确定，可能与北方某个表示「强壮」的词有关。

items.en: The word seems to have spread from the north of England, where a related form meant strong or bulky.
items.cn: 这个词似乎从英格兰北部传开，那里一个相关形式表示「强壮、粗大」。

items.en: Older English used great and large for size, and big was at first a plain everyday word.
items.cn: 古英语用 great 与 large 表示「大」，而 big 起初只是个朴素的日常词。

items.en: From bodily size the word spread to importance, to age, and to abstract amount.
items.cn: 从身体的尺寸出发，这个词扩展到重要性、年龄和抽象的数量。

items.en: Today big is one of the commonest adjectives, and its comparison is bigger and biggest.
items.cn: 今天 big 是最常用的形容词之一，比较级是 bigger，最高级是 biggest。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the comparison forms and short rhyming words; the near-meaning group collects other words for large.
note.cn: 形近组收比较级形式与押韵的短词；近义组收其他表示「大」的词。

entries.definition: The comparative of big, meaning more large.
entries.definitionCN: big 的比较级，义为「更大的」。

entries.definition: The superlative of big, meaning the most large.
entries.definitionCN: big 的最高级，义为「最大的」。

entries.definition: A farm animal kept for meat; it rhymes with big.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「猪」，与 big 押韵。

entries.definition: To break up and move earth; it rhymes with big.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「挖」，与 big 押韵。

entries.definition: Great in size or amount, often slightly more formal than big.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「大的」，往往比 big 稍正式。

entries.definition: Very large, or very important and admired.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「巨大的」，也指「伟大的」。

entries.definition: Extremely large, stronger than big.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「巨大的」，比 big 语气更强。

entries.definition: Little in size; the direct opposite of the first sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「小的」，是第一个义项的直接反义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded history, the real comparisons, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的历史、真实的比较级形式和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Big came from the north of England and meant strong and bulky before it meant simply large.
normal.cn: big 来自英格兰北部，先表示「强壮、粗大」，后来才单纯表示「大」。

normal.en: Its deeper origin is uncertain, so learn the word through its modern family instead.
normal.cn: 它更早的来源不确定，所以改从现代词族来记这个词。

normal.en: The comparison doubles the g: bigger, biggest.
normal.cn: 比较级要双写 g：bigger、biggest。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with problem, brother, deal and city.
normal.cn: 它常与 problem、brother、deal、city 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-i-g; only three letters, and the final g doubles before -er.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-i-g，只有三个字母，加 -er 时末尾的 g 要双写。

abstract.en: See an elephant beside a row of small birds: the gap in height is the meaning.
abstract.cn: 想象一头大象站在一排小鸟旁边，高度上的差距就是这个词的意思。

abstract.en: Shrink the elephant into a decision and then into a dream: the same size word covers weight, importance and ambition.
abstract.cn: 把大象缩成一个决定，再缩成一个梦想：同一个尺寸词覆盖分量、重要性和抱负。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the elephant bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让那头大象把意思带回来。

examples.en: An elephant is a very big animal.
examples.cn: 大象是一种很大的动物。

examples.en: Moving house is a big decision.
examples.cn: 搬家是一个重大的决定。

examples.en: My big brother is at university.
examples.cn: 我哥哥在上大学。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「逼格」——排场很大才显得有格：大的

root: big 见于中古英语，更早的来源不确定，一般认为与英格兰北部某个表示「强壮、粗大」的词有关。它先表示身体粗大，再扩展到重要性、年龄、抽象数量与抱负，逐渐取代了 great、large 在口语中的地位。比较级 bigger 与最高级 biggest 都要双写 g。

sensesIntro.en: All five senses of big grow from one picture: something that takes up more space, whether in the body, in attention, in years, in amount, or in ambition.
sensesIntro.cn: big 的五个义项都从同一幅画面长出来：某物占据更多空间，无论在身体上、注意力上、年岁上、数量上，还是抱负上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an elephant standing beside a row of small birds
core.cn: 核心意象：一头大象站在一排小鸟旁边

branches.en: THE BODY: the plainest sense is taking up much room.
branches.cn: 身体线：最朴素的义项就是占据很大空间。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT: what fills the eye also fills the mind, so big means important.
branches.cn: 分量线：占满视线的东西也占满心思，所以 big 表示「重要」。

branches.en: THE YEARS: the larger child in a family is also the older one.
branches.cn: 年岁线：家里个子更大的孩子也正是年长的那个。

definition_zh: 自行车（口语）；摩托车（口语）；骑自行车
definition_en: a bicycle or motorcycle, or to ride one
core_image: 一辆被随手靠在墙边的旧自行车
scene: 校门口的墙边停着一排自行车，孩子们正在找自己的那一辆。My bike is the red one by the gate.
sceneCN: 这里 bike 是「自行车」（第 1 个义项：口语中对自行车的简称）；句意为我的自行车是门口那辆红色的。

senses.title: A bicycle, in everyday speech
senses.definition: a bicycle, used in ordinary and informal speech

senses.example: My bike is the red one by the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 我的自行车是门口那辆红色的。
senses.why: Bike is a clipped form of bicycle, and clipping is the usual way English shortens a long borrowed word for everyday use.

senses.title: A motorcycle, in everyday speech
senses.definition: a motorcycle, especially in informal speech where motorbike is shortened to bike
senses.definitionCN: 摩托车，尤见于把 motorbike 缩成 bike 的非正式口语

senses.why: The same short form was applied to motorbike, so bike covers both machines and only context tells them apart.

senses.title: To ride a bike

senses.example: We biked along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 我们沿着河边骑车。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb in the ordinary English way, so to bike is simply to use the machine the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 名词按英语常见方式转成动词，所以 to bike 就是用这个名词所指的车行动。

intro.en: Bike is not an old word but a clipped form of bicycle, and the clipping spread to motorbike.
intro.cn: bike 不是古老的词，而是 bicycle 的截短形式，这一截短又扩展到了 motorbike。

items.en: Bike was shortened from bicycle in everyday speech in the late nineteenth century.
items.cn: bike 是十九世纪后期日常口语从 bicycle 截短而来的。

items.en: Speakers cut long borrowed words down to one syllable whenever the meaning stays clear.
items.cn: 只要意思仍然清楚，说话人就会把冗长的外来词砍成一个音节。

items.en: The same short form was applied to motorbike, so bike came to cover both machines.
items.cn: 同一个简短形式也被用到 motorbike 上，于是 bike 覆盖了两种车。

items.en: From the noun came the verb to bike, meaning to ride such a machine.
items.cn: 由名词产生动词 to bike，表示骑这种车。

items.en: Today bike is the ordinary word in speech, while bicycle stays the formal one.
items.cn: 今天 bike 是口语里的普通说法，而 bicycle 仍是正式用词。

normal.cn: 拼写是 b-i-k-e：一个长元音，末尾的 e 不发音。

definition_zh: 垃圾箱；储物箱；扔掉（口语）
definition_en: a container for waste or for storing things
core_image: 一个方正的塑料箱，盖子半开，里面装着要丢掉的东西
scene: 厨房角落的垃圾箱已经满了，妈妈让孩子把它拿出去倒掉。Please put the paper in the bin.
sceneCN: 这里 bin 是「垃圾箱」（第 1 个义项：装废弃物的容器）；句意为请把纸放进垃圾箱。

senses.title: A container for waste
senses.definition: a container into which rubbish is thrown
senses.definitionCN: 用来扔废弃物的容器
senses.example: Please put the paper in the bin.
senses.exampleCN: 请把纸放进垃圾箱。
senses.why: Old English bin named a box or a receptacle, often for grain; when waste became a daily matter, the same word attached to the box that holds it.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 bin 指箱、槽，多用来装谷物；当垃圾成为日常事务后，同一个词就附到了装垃圾的箱子上。

senses.title: A storage box
senses.definition: a large container used for storing goods, such as grain, fruit, or coal
senses.definitionCN: 用来存放货物的大箱子，如装谷物、水果或煤的箱子
senses.example: The apples are stored in a wooden bin.
senses.exampleCN: 苹果存放在一个木箱里。
senses.why: Storage is the oldest job of the bin, so this sense simply keeps the original use of the word alive.
senses.whyCN: 储物是 bin 最古老的用途，所以这个义项只是让这个词最初的用法活下来。

senses.title: To throw something away
senses.definition: to throw something away, used in informal British speech
senses.definitionCN: 把某物丢掉，用于非正式的英式口语
senses.example: He binned the old magazines.
senses.exampleCN: 他把旧杂志扔掉了。
senses.why: The verb is the noun in action: putting something into the waste bin, which in speech simply means discarding it.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词在行动：把东西放进垃圾箱，在口语里就简化成「丢掉」。

intro.en: Bin is an old English word for a box, and its link to a Latin basket word is suggested but not certain.
intro.cn: bin 是英语里古老的「箱子」用词，它与拉丁语「篮子」一词的关系有人提出，但不确定。

items.en: Old English bin named a box or a receptacle, especially one for grain or stores.
items.cn: 古英语 bin 指箱子或容器，尤其是装谷物与货物的那种。

items.en: A similar Latin word benna meant a basket, and the two may be related, though this is not certain.
items.cn: 拉丁语中有一个相似的词 benna 表示篮子，二者可能有关，但并不确定。

items.en: The word stayed in use for storage containers of many kinds through the Middle English period.
items.cn: 在中古英语时期，这个词一直用于各种储物容器。

items.en: As rubbish became a daily concern, the container for it took the same name and bin became the usual word for a waste box.
items.cn: 随着垃圾成为日常问题，装垃圾的容器也用了同一个名字，bin 于是成为「垃圾箱」的常用词。

items.en: Today bin covers waste bins, storage bins, and even the act of throwing something away in speech.
items.cn: 今天 bin 可指垃圾箱、储物箱，口语里甚至可指「扔掉」这个动作。

note.cn: 形近组收押韵或读音相近的短词；近义组收其他容器与垃圾用词。

normal.en: Old English bin meant a storage box, and that sense still lives in a wooden bin for apples.
normal.cn: 古英语 bin 指储物箱，这个义项至今活在装苹果的木箱里。

normal.en: Latin benna meant a basket, and the link to bin is possible but not certain.
